paras.zh: 以下就是他们对其主观结论的描述。

paras.en: METR: In our first section, we share our subjective conclusions about risk. We now believe that:
paras.zh: METR：在第一节中，我们分享关于风险的主观结论。我们现在认为：

paras.en: *   As of October 2026, Anthropic is likely improving the capabilities of their models on well-specified tasks at around twice the rate they did between March 2024 and October 2025. This estimate is given with high uncertainty; we would not be surprised if the true acceleration was closer to 1.3x or 3x the historical rate.
paras.zh: *   截至 2026 年 10 月，Anthropic 在定义明确的任务上提升其模型能力的速度，可能约为其在 2024 年 3 月至 2025 年 10 月期间的两倍。这一估计具有很高的不确定性；如果真实的加速幅度更接近历史速率的 1.3 倍或 3 倍，我们也不会感到意外。

paras.en: *   A majority of this acceleration today is likely attributable to Anthropic's extensive use of AI to do R&D, though there is significant uncertainty and other causes likely played a large role in acceleration in late 2025.
paras.zh: *   如今这种加速的大部分可能归因于 Anthropic 大量使用 AI 进行研发，尽管存在显著的不确定性，且其他因素很可能在 2025 年末的加速中发挥了重要作用。

paras.en: *   The lack of observed bottlenecks or strong diminishing returns means there is a significant risk that further capabilities progress could lead to even faster acceleration, though, as we say below, we may be missing important bottlenecks.
paras.zh: *   未观察到瓶颈或强烈的收益递减，这意味着存在显著风险：进一步的能力进步可能导致更快的加速；不过，正如我们在下文所述，我们可能遗漏了重要的瓶颈。

paras.en: *   Since October 2025, benchmark scores (measured via AECI, Anthropic's version of the Epoch Capabilities Index) for Anthropic's models have been growing at an estimated 1.9x the pre-October 2025 rate [95% confidence interval: 1.5–2.8x], implying that Anthropic has made roughly two years of historical progress over the last year.
paras.zh: *   自 2025 年 10 月以来，Anthropic 模型的基准分数（通过 AECI，即 Anthropic 版本的 Epoch Capabilities Index 衡量）估计以 2025 年 10 月之前速率的 1.9 倍增长 [95% 置信区间：1.5–2.8 倍]，这意味着 Anthropic 在过去一年中取得了大约相当于历史上两年的进展。

paras.en: *   We are confident that the acceleration was not due to an acceleration in the scaling of training compute.
paras.zh: *   我们确信，这一加速并非源于训练算力 Scaling（规模扩张）的加速。

paras.en: *   Interviews and surveys are consistent with AI usage causing a doubling in the pace of capabilities progress. Anthropic staff self-report dramatic uplift from use of AI systems in interviews and surveys, although these are challenging to interpret. We were told that R&D is accelerated primarily via AI assistance rather than fully autonomous contributions, but there are some signs that fully autonomous contributions will play a larger role soon.
paras.zh: *   访谈和调查与 AI 使用导致能力进展速度翻倍这一结论相一致。Anthropic 员工在访谈和调查中自我报告称，使用 AI 系统带来了显著提升，尽管这些报告难以解读。我们被告知，研发的加速主要通过 AI 辅助而非完全自主的贡献实现，但有一些迹象表明，完全自主的贡献将在不久后发挥更大的作用。

paras.en: *   We did not see evidence for significant bottlenecks which would prevent further capabilities progress due to limits on algorithmic progress, training compute, experiment compute, or data in the next 12 months. However, our understanding of the status of different bottlenecks changed several times as we received more detailed information, so we are not confident in our current assessment.
paras.zh: *   我们没有看到证据表明，在未来 12 个月内，算法进展、训练算力、实验算力或数据方面的限制会造成显著瓶颈，从而阻碍能力的进一步进展。然而，随着我们获得更详细的信息，我们对不同瓶颈状况的理解发生了多次变化，因此我们对当前的评估并不确信。

items.en: The goal of the report was to measure acceleration of Anthropic's internal growth rate, how much of that acceleration is due to AI R&D, and whether there exist any important bottlenecks to further acceleration. This requires a lot of sensitive data, and they got most of what they requested.
items.zh: 该报告的目标是衡量 Anthropic 内部增长率的加速情况、其中有多少加速来自 AI 研发，以及进一步加速是否存在任何重要瓶颈。这需要大量敏感数据，而他们获得了所要求的大部分数据。

items.en: A detailed description of the data we had access to was redacted. A summarized version is as follows:
items.zh: 对我们所获取数据的详细描述已被删节。摘要版本如下：

items.en: 1. Internal benchmark scores and AECI for internal models, plus sample tasks, rubric answers, and agent expenditure on those tasks.
items.zh: 1. 内部模型的内部基准分数与 AECI，以及样本任务、评分标准答案和智能体在这些任务上的支出。

items.en: 2. Historical data on algorithmic efficiency and overall model strength in pretraining and RL, as well as improvements to compute utilization, inference efficiency, and data efficiency.
items.zh: 2. 关于算法效率以及预训练和强化学习中整体模型强度的历史数据，还有算力利用率、推理效率和数据效率方面的改进。

items.en: 3. Headcount and attribution of progress to specific staff.
items.zh: 3. 人员数量以及将进展归因于具体员工的情况。

items.en: 4. Training compute metrics in many relevant domains.
items.zh: 4. 在多个相关领域中的训练算力指标。

items.en: 5. Internal analysis on relevant open questions.
items.zh: 5. 针对相关开放问题的内部分析。

items.en: 6. Internal surveys of self-reported AI uplift by team.
items.zh: 6. 按团队开展的自报 AI 提升幅度的内部调查。

items.en: 7. Lines of code and pull requests across the company and some research teams.
items.zh: 7. 全公司及部分研究团队的代码行数与拉取请求数。

items.en: 8. AI agent inference spend over time.
items.zh: 8. AI 智能体推理支出随时间的变化。

items.en: 9. Internal documents on autonomous research contributions.
items.zh: 9. 关于自主研究贡献的内部文件。

items.en: 10. ~15 interviews with key staff, covering a predefined but wide scope that excluded particularly sensitive topics.
items.zh: 10. 约 15 次对关键员工的访谈，覆盖一个预先设定但范围广泛的议题，其中排除了特别敏感的话题。

items.en: In a small number of cases, Anthropic did not provide relevant information when they deemed it too sensitive.
items.zh: 在少数情况下，Anthropic 认为相关信息过于敏感，因而未予提供。

items.en: Anthropic also offered extensive staff time and expertise to this project. We believe the two staff we worked most closely with are the two highest-context researchers on AI R&D acceleration measurement at Anthropic. Both of these staff met with us frequently for live discussion, and spent substantial time collecting data, doing analysis, and providing feedback.
items.zh: Anthropic 还为该项目投入了大量员工时间与专业知识。我们认为，与我们合作最密切的两位员工是 Anthropic 内部在 AI 研发加速测量方面背景知识最丰富的研究者。这两位员工频繁与我们进行实时讨论，并花费大量时间收集数据、开展分析以及提供反馈。

items.en: In exchange, Anthropic could redact anything in the report. They did so, aggressively.
items.zh: 作为交换，Anthropic 可以删节报告中的任何内容。他们确实这样做了，而且删节力度很大。

items.en: METR’s only recourse is that it can then share its level of access, that things had been redacted, and whether findings depend on redacted information. Which they do. The majority of the most informative evidence is redacted.
items.zh: METR 的唯一办法是，它可以随后分享其访问级别、哪些内容已被删节，以及研究结果是否依赖于被删节的信息。而事实确实如此。大多数最具信息量的证据都被删节了。

items.en: METR: We submitted a ~100-page full report on our assessment to Anthropic. For the public version, Anthropic redacted a majority of the evidence we found most informative. As a consequence, the public must rely on our judgment more than we consider ideal.
items.zh: METR：我们向 Anthropic 提交了一份约 100 页的完整评估报告。在公开版本中，Anthropic 删节了我们发现的大多数最具信息量的证据。因此，公众必须比我们认为理想情况更依赖我们的判断。

items.capEn: Some of these redactions seem clearly appropriate. Others seem questionable.
items.capZh: 其中一些涂黑似乎明显合理。另一些似乎可疑。

items.en: METR: While we were able to freely share our highest-level conclusions about risk, Anthropic redacted a majority of the evidence we found most informative for these conclusions. Anthropic described the redactions as “aimed at removing confidential information that could accelerate other AI developers.”
items.zh: METR：虽然我们能够自由分享关于风险的最高层结论，但 Anthropic 删节了我们发现的、对这些结论最具信息量的大多数证据。Anthropic 将删节描述为“旨在移除可能加速其他 AI 开发者的机密信息”。

items.en: Some of these redactions are themselves challenging to describe clearly without revealing sensitive information we have been asked to redact.
items.zh: 其中一些删节本身难以在不透露我们被要求删节的敏感信息的情况下清晰描述。

items.en: We share a table of important evidence we were and were not able to discuss given the redactions in our process section below. All redactions that were important for our conclusions are covered by our descriptions in that table or other in-line descriptions in the report below.
items.zh: 我们在下面的过程部分中分享了一个表格，列出了鉴于删节我们能够和无法讨论的重要证据。所有对我们的结论重要的删节都已被该表格中的描述或下面报告中的其他行内描述所涵盖。

items.en: Much of the redacted evidence we viewed had multiple plausible interpretations, and both METR and Anthropic researchers have significant uncertainty about how to synthesize the evidence into a holistic picture. This makes it hard for the public to judge this evidence themselves, reconcile it with evidence from other sources, and come to their own conclusions (i.e., this report does not achieve 'transparency about evidence'). As a consequence, the public has to rely on METR's judgment much more than would be ideal, given the weight of the questions answered here.
items.zh: 我们查看的许多被删节的证据有多种合理的解释，METR 和 Anthropic 的研究人员对于如何将这些证据综合成一个整体图景存在很大的不确定性。这使得公众难以自行判断这些证据，难以将其与其他来源的证据相协调，并得出自己的结论（即本报告未能实现“证据透明”）。因此，鉴于此处所回答问题的分量，公众不得不比理想情况下更多地依赖 METR 的判断。

items.en: METR: Anthropic's redactions also meant that we could not communicate:
items.zh: METR：Anthropic 的删节也意味着我们无法传达：

items.en: 1. Our more detailed estimates of acceleration and attribution to AI usage for key areas of the model training pipeline.
items.zh: 1. 我们对模型训练流程关键领域的加速及其归因于 AI 使用的更详细估计。

items.en: 2. Our more detailed breakdown of progress attributable to compute, data and algorithmic progress, other than the key takeaway that "We are confident that the acceleration was not due to acceleration in training compute."
items.zh: 2. 我们对算力、数据和算法进展所归因的进步的更详细分解，除了关键结论“我们确信加速并非由于训练算力的加速”之外。

items.en: 3. More detailed answers to the limitations questions in our proposal, which would require more discussion of methodological details.
items.zh: 3. 对我们提案中局限性问题的更详细回答，这将需要更多关于方法细节的讨论。

items.en: 4. Forecasts of metrics for future models.
items.zh: 4. 对未来模型指标的预测。

items.en: They also made some other, more minor redactions throughout, which we attempt to describe in each section of this report.
items.zh: 他们还在全文中做了其他一些较为次要的删节，我们试图在本报告的每一节中加以说明。

items.en: Anthropic described the redactions as "aimed at removing confidential information that could accelerate other AI developers."
items.zh: Anthropic 将这些删节描述为“旨在移除可能加速其他 AI 开发者发展的机密信息”。

items.en: They also could not show us any use of METR's core accounting framework. We know the framework looks like this, but that's all we get:
items.zh: 他们也无法向我们展示 METR 核心核算框架的任何使用情况。我们知道该框架大致如下，但我们能得到的就只有这些：

items.en: This is one of the more annoying redactions. What are these non-AI factors? Candidates include compute scaling, hiring, data improvements, algorithmic discoveries and resolving other bottlenecks. Compute has been ruled out. But we don’t know how they view the other factors.
items.zh: 这是一处更令人恼火的删节。这些非 AI 因素是什么？候选包括算力扩张、招聘、数据改进、算法发现以及解决其他瓶颈。算力已被排除。但我们不知道他们如何看待其他因素。

items.en: 1. **The acceleration in late 2025 was likely influenced by non-AI factors.** We investigated a variety of factors which could have contributed to the observed acceleration in late 2025, but details of many of these factors have been redacted.
items.zh: 1. **2025 年末的加速可能受到非 AI 因素的影响。** 我们调查了多种可能促成 2025 年末观察到的加速的因素，但其中许多因素的细节已被删节。

items.en: 2. **We guess that a majority (perhaps ≈80%) of the current (October 2026) acceleration is due to AI.** This judgment is given with substantial uncertainty, but is based on a variety of lines of evidence on contributions from AI and other causes. We believe AI’s contribution has grown relatively more important over time, and do not think the other factors we investigated would explain the sustained acceleration. The evidence of speedup from the usage of AI we describe below also seems compatible with a large contribution.
items.zh: 2. **我们猜测当前（2026 年 10 月）加速的大部分（或许约 80%）归因于 AI。** 这一判断具有相当大的不确定性，但基于关于 AI 和其他原因贡献的多种证据。我们认为 AI 的贡献随时间相对变得更加重要，并且不认为我们调查的其他因素能解释持续的加速。下文描述的 AI 使用带来加速的证据似乎也与大贡献相符。

items.en: The non-AI acceleration continues, supplemented by the AI-driven one:
items.zh: 非 AI 加速仍在继续，并得到 AI 驱动加速的补充：

items.capEn: Thus they illustrate how to think about all three numbers: The historic trend, the counterfactual no-AI trend and the observed trend that includes use of AI.
items.capZh: 因此它们说明了如何思考所有三个数字：历史趋势、反事实的无 AI 趋势以及包含 AI 使用的观察趋势。

paras.en: The Risk Report introduced Model 1 and Model 2. Now we meet 3 and 4, and also 5.
paras.zh: 《风险报告》介绍了 Model 1 和 Model 2。现在我们来看 Model 3 和 Model 4，以及 Model 5。

paras.en: This includes the following models (these are the codenames shared with us; we understand they have different internal codenames):
paras.zh: 这包括以下模型（这些是提供给我们的代号；我们了解到它们有不同的内部代号）：

paras.en: *   Unreleased 2022, which finished training in 2022
paras.zh: *   未发布的 2022 模型，于 2022 年完成训练

paras.en: *   Model 2, which finished training in July 2026
paras.zh: *   Model 2，于 2026 年 7 月完成训练

paras.en: *   Model 3, which finished training in August–September 2026
paras.zh: *   Model 3，于 2026 年 8 月至 9 月完成训练

paras.en: *   Model 4, which finished training in September–October 2026
paras.zh: *   模型 4，其训练于 2026 年 9 月至 10 月完成

paras.en: METR's Full Report includes a forecast for a future model, but this was redacted.
paras.zh: METR 的完整报告包含对一款未来模型的预测，但该部分已被涂黑（redacted）。

paras.en: If this is consistent, it seems like the clear correct way:
paras.zh: 如果这一点是一致的，那么它似乎就是明确正确的做法：

paras.en: METR: We use the date at which the model could be used by most Anthropic employees instead of public release dates; this allows us to make apples-to-apples comparisons with unreleased models. These in general show slightly higher degrees of acceleration as Anthropic is holding onto more recent models for slightly longer before their public release.
paras.zh: METR：我们采用模型可供大多数 Anthropic 员工使用的日期，而非公开发布日期；这使我们能够与未发布模型进行同类比较。总体而言，这些比较显示出略高的加速程度，因为 Anthropic 在公开发布之前会将较新的模型多保留一段时间。

paras.en: OpenAI used to hold onto models for a longer time. Then it got shorter. Whereas after Mythos, various forces are now holding models back for longer, including the desire to keep an advantage in R&D.
paras.zh: OpenAI 过去会将模型保留更长时间。后来这一时间变短了。而在 Mythos 之后，各种力量如今正将模型保留更长时间，包括希望保持研发优势的意愿。

paras.en: There are different reasons one might want to measure 'leads' or rates of progress. If you are measuring for commercial purposes, you care mostly about practical questions of what a public customer can do when. If you are measuring to predict RSI, you care about a very different measurement, and what you care about are internal capabilities, and ability to use them to make progress at the frontier.
paras.zh: 人们可能出于不同原因想要衡量“领先幅度”或进展速度。如果是为了商业目的而衡量，你主要关心的是公共客户在何时能做什么这一实际问题。如果是为了预测 RSI 而衡量，你关心的则是一种非常不同的度量，你关心的是内部能力，以及利用这些能力在前沿取得进展的能力。

paras.en: By that measure, things are picking up faster, and also the gaps are wider. If you believe in what this report is telling us, these are the measurements that count.
paras.zh: 按照这一度量，进展正在加快，而且差距也在扩大。如果你相信这份报告告诉我们的内容，那么这些才是真正重要的度量。

full.sec: What Could Possibly Have Gone Wrong?

paras.en: There are a number of ways this could be wrong, or be less than ideally accurate.
paras.zh: 这一判断可能存在多种出错方式，或者其准确性未达到理想水平。

paras.en: The biggest issue is limited access to data. Not all data requests were accepted, and there are many documents and other information sources that were not available.
paras.zh: 最大的问题是数据获取受限。并非所有数据请求都获得批准，而且有许多文档和其他信息来源无法获取。

paras.en: METR might have missed further acceleration, or AECI could underestimate capability growth, or automation could be closer.
paras.zh: METR 可能遗漏了进一步的加速，或者 AECI 可能低估了能力增长，又或者自动化程度可能更接近现实。

paras.en: On the other hand, perhaps there are non-AI factors that were missed that explain past acceleration, or historical growth was unusually low, creating the illusion of fundamental acceleration. Or perhaps acceleration could only work on a narrow set of tasks.
paras.zh: 另一方面，也许存在被遗漏的非 AI 因素可以解释过去的加速，或者历史增长异常低，从而造成了根本性加速的错觉。又或者，加速可能只适用于一小部分任务。

paras.en: I notice that the upside risks and downside risks of the estimate are asymmetrical. We have three in each direction, but they don't match (Opus 5.5 says some of these do cancel out, but I don't think they fully do, and others clearly don't):
paras.zh: 我注意到该估计的上行风险与下行风险并不对称。两个方向各有三项，但它们并不匹配（Opus 5.5 认为其中一些会相互抵消，但我认为它们并未完全抵消，而另一些显然没有）：

paras.en: 1. Acceleration might be missed but not illusory.
paras.zh: 1. 加速可能被遗漏，但并非虚幻。

paras.en: 2. AECI could underestimate effective growth but not overestimate it, although elsewhere they do discuss error in both directions.
paras.zh: 2. AECI 可能低估有效增长，但不会高估它，尽管他们在别处确实讨论了两个方向的误差。

paras.en: 3. Automation could be closer but not farther away.
paras.zh: 3. 自动化可能更近，但不会更远。

paras.en: 4. Historical growth might be unusually low, but not unusually high.
paras.zh: 4. 历史增长可能异常低，但不会异常高。

paras.en: 5. Acceleration could be narrower, but not broader.
paras.zh: 5. 加速可能更窄，但不会更广。

paras.en: 6. Non-AI factors could be underestimated but not overestimated.
paras.zh: 6. 非 AI 因素可能被低估，但不会被高估。

paras.en: Curves on such things do not have to be symmetrical, so long as the average results of all of them are incorporated. This doesn't have to be an error. I do still wonder.
paras.zh: 这类曲线不必是对称的，只要将它们所有结果的平均值纳入考虑即可。这未必是一个错误。我确实仍存疑虑。

items.en: The main metric METR uses for this report is the Anthropic fork of the Epoch Capabilities Index, AECI.
items.zh: METR 在本报告中采用的主要指标是 Epoch Capabilities Index 的 Anthropic 分支版本，即 AECI。

items.en: AECI is a measure of practical capability. Growth in AECI is multiplicative of odds of success on a task rather than linear, so linear progress on AECI means more than you might think:
items.zh: AECI 是一种衡量实际能力的指标。AECI 的增长是任务成功几率的乘性增长而非线性增长，因此 AECI 上的线性进展意味着比你想象中更多的东西：

items.en: Charles Foster (METR): It's easy to mistake linear gains in ECI for linear gains in model performance. Each additional point actually *multiplies* a model's odds of success on every benchmark. For example, historically each 5-point increase in ECI corresponded to roughly a doubling in time horizon.
items.zh: Charles Foster（METR）：人们很容易把 ECI 的线性增益误认为模型性能的线性增益。实际上，每增加一分都会*成倍*提高模型在每个基准上的成功几率。例如，从历史上看，ECI 每提高 5 分，大致对应时间跨度翻倍。

items.en: METR focused a lot on the question of whether the metrics are biased or consistent.
items.zh: METR 大量关注了这些指标是否存在偏差或是否一致的问题。

items.en: METR: These investigations included attempts to understand:
items.zh: METR：这些调查包括尝试理解以下问题：

items.en: 1. Different methodological variants of internal metrics. We spent multiple weeks on these investigations, and this is our greatest source of uncertainty.
items.zh: 1. 内部指标的不同方法学变体。我们在这些调查上花费了数周时间，这是我们最大的不确定性来源。

items.en: 2. The beliefs of staff on the relevant teams about key internal evidence and estimates of acceleration.
items.zh: 2. 相关团队员工对关键内部证据和加速估计的看法。

items.en: 3. Whether other parts of the model training pipeline could be biasing our estimates of acceleration, and where adjustments could be applied.
items.zh: 3. 模型训练流程的其他部分是否可能使我们对加速的估计产生偏差，以及可以在何处进行调整。

items.en: 4. Whether Anthropic could be overfitting to internal metrics.
items.zh: 4. Anthropic 是否可能对内部指标过拟合。

items.en: The measurements are also robust to choice of included benchmarks, and to which model snapshots are included, and to regularization.
items.zh: 这些测量对纳入基准的选择、纳入哪些模型快照以及正则化也都是稳健的。

items.en: If non-Anthropic models are included, then the estimate of acceleration goes down to 1.4x.
items.zh: 如果纳入非 Anthropic 的模型，那么加速的估计值会降至 1.4 倍。

items.en: METR suggests as another potential justification for lower acceleration rates that Anthropic’s models underperformed on benchmarks in the earlier period relative to their true capabilities, which matches my understanding.
items.zh: METR 提出了另一个可能解释加速率较低的理由：Anthropic 的模型在早期阶段相对于其真实能力在基准测试上表现不佳，这与我的理解一致。

items.en: I would also suggest that if Anthropic was previously behind, then being behind makes progress easier via fast following, even if you cannot distill.
items.zh: 我还想指出，如果 Anthropic 之前处于落后状态，那么落后会通过快速跟随使进展更容易，即使你无法进行蒸馏。

items.en: There are some potential issues with AECI:
items.zh: AECI 存在一些潜在问题：

items.en: 1. We go into detail on potential problems with AECI such as:
items.zh: 1. 我们详细讨论了 AECI 的潜在问题，例如：

items.en: 1. Anthropic's internal benchmarks are increasingly saturated: Model 4 achieves greater than 50% on all the AECI benchmarks on which it was tested. However, measured acceleration appears reasonably robust to saturation concerns.
items.zh: 1. Anthropic 的内部基准正日益饱和：Model 4 在其测试过的所有 AECI 基准上均达到 50% 以上。然而，所测得的加速似乎对饱和问题具有相当的稳健性。

items.en: 2. Token spend may be too low to maximally elicit models.
items.zh: 2. Token 消耗可能过低，无法最大程度地激发模型能力。

items.en: 3. The logistic link function could be misspecified on a few benchmarks. However, on the whole we think it is a reasonable approximation.
items.zh: 3. 逻辑链接函数在少数基准上可能存在设定错误。但总体而言，我们认为这是一个合理的近似。

items.en: 4. There are various reasons why an acceleration in benchmark scores could overstate or understate an acceleration in real-world impacts.
items.zh: 4. 基准分数的加速可能高估或低估现实世界影响的加速，原因有多种。

items.en: If AECI is going to serve as a measure of the capabilities of models, the first part of this must be true:
items.zh: 如果 AECI 要作为模型能力的度量，那么其第一部分必须成立：

items.en: AECI assumes that a model's score on a benchmark is a function of the model's latent strength, and specifically that the function is logistic (shown below in black).
items.zh: AECI 假设模型在基准上的得分是模型潜在强度的函数，并具体假设该函数为 logistic 函数（下图中以黑色显示）。

items.en: Any given metric then has to worry about S-curves and saturation points.
items.zh: 因此，任何给定的指标都必须考虑 S 形曲线和饱和点。

items.en: This can be interpreted as an assumption on the distribution of difficulty of tasks in a benchmark, including how many tasks are broken or what fraction can be guessed. The following figure illustrates a few different link functions. The logistic function assumes a symmetric distribution with exponentially declining tails. The log-log function assumes a long tail of hard tasks; the complementary log-log function assumes a long tail of easy tasks.
items.zh: 这可以解释为对基准中任务难度分布的假设，包括有多少任务是损坏的，或者有多大比例是可以猜对的。下图展示了几个不同的链接函数。logistic 函数假设一个对称分布，其尾部呈指数衰减。log-log 函数假设存在一个困难任务的长尾；互补 log-log 函数假设存在一个简单任务的长尾。

items.en: Depending on what type of curve you think this is, you get different measurements of the rate of acceleration. Unfortunately basically all the curve fits are similarly good at Out-of-sample \(R^2\). It makes sense to default to standard logistic, but this illustrates that in theory you can explain or justify a wide range of measurements.
items.zh: 取决于你认为这是哪种类型的曲线，你会得到不同的加速率测量结果。不幸的是，基本上所有曲线拟合在样本外 \(R^2\) 上表现同样好。默认采用标准 logistic 是合理的，但这说明理论上你可以解释或证明广泛的测量结果。

items.capEn: METR says they have no reason to prefer one of these over others. I would say they make distinct claims over the distribution of tasks. So if we want to know which is best, we should look at the tasks.
items.capZh: METR 表示他们没有理由偏好其中之一。我会说它们对任务分布做出了不同的主张。所以如果我们想知道哪个最好，我们应该看任务。

full.sec: The Public Information Alone Could Suggest Slower Speedup
full.secZh: 仅凭公开信息即可推断出更慢的加速

paras.en: In particular, if you are relying only on the AECI, one can selectively edit out the Mythos jump or consider part of this as catching up on relative compute allocation.
paras.zh: 特别是，如果仅依赖 AECI，人们可以选择性地剔除 Mythos 跃升，或将其部分视为在相对算力分配上的追赶。

paras.en: Toby Ord: I don't think 2x is the best interpretation of this data. It assumes zero level shift from the new Mythos pre-train. If you allow for a level shift from that as well as a slope change, the slope change drops to about 1.4x.
paras.zh: Toby Ord：我认为 2 倍并不是对这批数据的最佳解读。它假设新的 Mythos 预训练没有带来水平位移。如果同时允许水平位移和斜率变化，斜率变化会降至约 1.4 倍。

paras.en: METR has released a very interesting report suggesting a recent acceleration in AI capabilities this year at Anthropic due to RSI.
paras.zh: METR 发布了一份非常有趣的报告，指出今年 Anthropic 的 AI 能力因 RSI 而出现近期加速。

paras.en: But they can't confidently reject an alternative explanation: the step change you get with the larger pre-train of Mythos.
paras.zh: 但他们无法有把握地排除另一种解释：更大规模的 Mythos 预训练所带来的阶跃变化。

paras.en: Woody Lee: It looks like Anthropic was running behind the composite frontier, so the speedup in relation to that is 1.4x. Not sure if this changed any analysis, but it shows that using just the ant baseline may give a different number.
paras.zh: Woody Lee：看起来 Anthropic 当时落后于综合前沿，因此相对于该前沿的加速为 1.4 倍。不确定这是否改变了任何分析，但它表明仅使用 ant 基线可能会得出不同的数字。

paras.en: There are two responses to this. One is that there is private redacted information that is factoring into the reports.
paras.zh: 对此有两种回应。其一是有未公开的删节信息被纳入了报告。

paras.en: Buck Shlegeris: Toby's analysis totally misses the point here IMO. He's right that the graph of capabilities over time could be explained as a one-off jump in capabilities from the Mythos pretrain. But that graph is not the main reason why METR thinks AI R&D is now sped up 1.7x by AI. The graph is just the only part of their analysis that wasn't redacted.
paras.zh: Buck Shlegeris：在我看来，Toby 的分析完全没抓住重点。他说得对，能力随时间变化的图表可以解释为 Mythos 预训练带来的一次性能力跃升。但该图表并不是 METR 认为 AI 研发现在被 AI 加速了 1.7 倍的主要原因。图表只是他们分析中唯一未被删节的部分。

paras.en: They say that "a majority (perhaps ≈80%) of the current (October 2026) acceleration is due to AI", based on "a variety of lines of evidence on contributions from AI and other causes", after saying that "[t]he acceleration in late 2025 was likely influenced by non-AI factors."
paras.zh: 他们表示，“当前（2026 年 10 月）加速的大部分（可能约 80%）归因于 AI”，依据是“关于 AI 和其他因素贡献的多种证据”，此前他们还说过“2025 年末的加速可能受到非 AI 因素的影响”。

paras.en: METR's report makes it clear that they considered Toby's hypothesis and rejected it for redacted reasons, rather than failing to consider it, in the appendix "New internal models make a permanent slope change look more plausible than a one-time jump at Mythos Preview."
paras.zh: METR 的报告明确表示，他们考虑了 Toby 的假设，并因删节原因而拒绝，而非未考虑，在附录“新的内部模型使永久斜率变化比 Mythos Preview 的一次性跃升看起来更合理”中。

paras.en: It totally makes sense to worry that METR's analysis is wrong. It's definitely unfortunate that the main evidence they were allowed to share does not suffice to demonstrate their point, for this reason among others. But I don't think it makes sense to consider Toby's argument a knockdown argument against the report's conclusion, because the conclusion wasn't mostly derived from the observations whose interpretation Toby disputes. See [here].
paras.zh: 担心 METR 的分析有误是完全合理的。不幸的是，他们被允许分享的主要证据不足以证明其观点，原因之一就在于此。但我认为，将 Toby 的论点视为对报告结论的致命反驳并不合理，因为该结论主要并非源自 Toby 所质疑其解释的观察结果。参见[此处]。

paras.en: The other response is that such modifications are selective. Yes, if you take away whatever the biggest discontinuous improvement is over a period, you will see slower returns. Yes, Anthropic's position in compute consumption relative to others has shifted. But once we go down such roads, why do we think similar shifts will not happen again?
paras.zh: 另一种回应是，这类修改具有选择性。是的，如果你去掉某一时期内最大的不连续改进，你就会看到回报变慢。是的，Anthropic 相对于其他方在算力消耗上的位置已经发生了变化。但一旦我们走上这条路，我们凭什么认为类似的转变不会再次发生？

paras.en: There is always temptation to extrapolate a future without such jumps. You don't get to do that. The baseline scenario contains outliers and jumps.
paras.zh: 人们总是倾向于外推一个没有此类跃升的未来。但你不能这样做。基线情景本身就包含离群值和跃升。

paras.en: We can only reject the Mythos upshift if we have strong reason to believe we won't be able to do any similar things again. I don't see why that would be true.
paras.zh: 只有当我们有强有力的理由相信我们再也无法做出任何类似的事情时，我们才能否定 Mythos 上移。我看不出为什么这会是成立的。

items.en: It is poised to soon escalate far more quickly. This fact is overdetermined. There are even 'signs of life' of areas of potentially full automation. The details are less clear.
items.zh: 它即将以快得多的速度升级。这一事实是多重因素共同决定的。甚至已经出现了可能实现完全自动化的领域的“生命迹象”。具体细节则不那么清晰。

items.en: METR: We define AI speedup as the ratio between a staff member or team's output with AI and without AI, noting that output can often be difficult to measure or define.
items.zh: METR：我们将 AI 加速定义为一名员工或团队在有 AI 与无 AI 情况下的产出之比，并指出产出往往难以衡量或定义。

items.en: We now briefly survey the overall evidence for AI speedup, concluding:
items.zh: 我们现在简要梳理关于 AI 加速的整体证据，并得出以下结论：

items.en: 1. There is some evidence for high speedup, though the precise amount of speedup is highly uncertain.
items.zh: 1. 有一些证据表明存在高加速，但加速的确切幅度高度不确定。

items.en: 2. Fully autonomous contributions to AI R&D are not currently a large contributor to overall progress, but they may be in the near future.
items.zh: 2. 目前，对 AI 研发的完全自主贡献并不是整体进展的主要贡献者，但在不久的将来可能会是。

items.en: … We have many lines of evidence relevant to AI's contribution to progress in different parts of the model training pipeline, including interviews, self-reported uplift, headcount, lines of code, experiment usage, and qualitative reflections from leadership. We highlight three important unredacted sources.
items.zh: ……我们掌握了许多证据，涉及 AI 在模型训练流程不同环节中对进展的贡献，包括访谈、自我报告的效率提升、人员编制、代码行数、实验使用情况以及领导层的定性反思。我们重点列出三个重要的未删节来源。

items.en: 1. Both METR and Anthropic interviewed many researchers in detail about the degree of overall acceleration in their area of work attributable to AI use (see details in the appendix below). Our overall impression was a quite wide range of estimates, but centered around a 2x acceleration.
items.zh: 1. METR 和 Anthropic 都详细访谈了许多研究人员，了解 AI 使用在其工作领域带来的整体加速程度（详见下文附录）。我们的总体印象是，估计值范围相当宽，但集中在约 2 倍加速附近。

items.en: 2. Anthropic also shared data on self-reported uplift due to AI from a variety of sources. The most recent data is from a series of Slack polls. … The responses reflect low-effort consideration. Nevertheless, we observe consistent growth in these self-reports, and very high levels (reaching 12x in October 2026), as shown in the chart below.
items.zh: 2. Anthropic 还分享了来自多种来源的、关于 AI 带来的自我报告效率提升的数据。最新数据来自一系列 Slack 投票。……这些回答反映的是低投入的考虑。尽管如此，我们观察到这些自我报告持续增长，且水平非常高（2026 年 10 月达到 12 倍），如下图所示。

items.en: 3. Researchers described significant "signs of life" implying [highly significant and fully autonomous] contributions could occur soon.
items.zh: 3. 研究人员描述了显著的“生命迹象”，暗示[高度显著且完全自主]的贡献可能很快出现。

items.capEn: The estimates here are a lot more than 2x in uplift for the employees, offset by slowness elsewhere, balancing out to 2x. Coding is dramatically more productive now.
items.capZh: 这里的估计对员工来说提升远不止 2 倍，被其他地方的缓慢所抵消，平衡后为 2 倍。编码现在的生产力显著提高。

items.en: Ajeya Cotra (METR): Importantly, **if AI is roughly doubling capabilities progress overall, it must be speeding up human researchers by** _**much**_ **more than that.**
items.zh: Ajeya Cotra（METR）：重要的是，**如果 AI 总体上使能力进展大约翻倍，那么它加速人类研究人员的幅度必然** _**远**_ **大于此。**

items.en: Ajeya Cotra (METR): researcher _labor_ is only one input to discovering these compute multipliers.
items.zh: Ajeya Cotra（METR）：研究人员的**劳动**只是发现这些算力倍增因素的其中一个输入。

items.en: … If we assume a very simple Cobb-Douglas model where experiment compute and labor are similarly important, that means the uplift to labor roughly needs to be the _square_ of the acceleration in compute multipliers.
items.zh: ……如果我们假设一个非常简单的 Cobb-Douglas 模型，其中实验算力和劳动同等重要，那意味着对劳动的提升大致需要是算力倍增加速的**平方**。

items.en: … This would imply that we would need a (~2-3x)^2 = ~4-9x speed up in labor to make overall AI capabilities go twice as fast.
items.zh: ……这意味着我们需要大约（~2-3x）^2 = ~4-9x 的劳动速度提升，才能使整体 AI 能力的发展速度翻倍。

items.en: They call this ‘broadly support AI doubling the growth rate’ but if we are going purely by the Claude sentiment analysis then the median answer was ‘borderline/unclear’.
items.zh: 他们称之为‘广泛支持 AI 使增长率翻倍’，但如果我们纯粹根据 Claude 的情感分析，那么中位数答案是‘临界/不明确’：

items.en: Both METR and Anthropic interviewed many researchers (see details in the following section). We used Claude to classify the quotes according to whether they support 2x or more acceleration from AI in their area of work, relative to working without AI. We interpret the results as mildly in favor of 2x or greater acceleration:
items.zh: METR 和 Anthropic 都采访了许多研究人员（详见下一节）。我们使用 Claude 对引述进行分类，判断它们是否支持在其工作领域中 AI 带来 2 倍或更多的加速（相对于没有 AI 的工作）。我们将结果解读为略微倾向于支持 2 倍或更大的加速：

items.en: *   Leans yes: 3
*   Borderline/unclear: 4
items.zh: *   边界/不明确：4

items.en: *   Leans no: 0
The quotes, with sensitive details redacted, are in the following section.
items.zh: 这些引文（敏感细节已隐去）见下一节。

items.en: The massive personal speedups are necessary to maintain the overall slower pace, so there is no inconsistency here. That's the frame for looking at the researcher quotes.
items.zh: 巨大的个人加速对于维持整体较慢的节奏是必要的，因此这里并不存在矛盾。这就是审视研究者引文的框架。

items.en: They roughly rank the researchers from the most gung-ho (A) to the least, and offer quotes. We start with the two ‘Yes’ votes.
items.zh: 他们大致按从最积极（A）到最不积极对研究人员进行了排名，并提供了引述。我们从两个“赞成”票开始。

items.en: A: I would definitely endorse >2 years of progress in 1 year and I don’t think 4 is crazy.
items.zh: A：我绝对会支持 1 年取得超过 2 年的进展，而且我认为 4 年也不算疯狂。

items.en: I think there’s some truth to the ‘we just started trying harder’ story, but IMO the bulk of the effect is recent models.
items.zh: 我认为“我们只是开始更努力了”的说法有一定道理，但在我看来，大部分效果来自最近的模型。

items.en: Like 80% reduction in time between idea and experiment, other 20% some mix of making fewer mistakes and being able to measure fiddly things that would’ve required too much one-off work before.
items.zh: 比如从想法到实验的时间减少了 80%，另外 20%是少犯错误和能够测量以前需要太多一次性工作的繁琐事情的混合效果。

items.en: I think there was a medium bump when it was good enough to code at all and a big bump with Opus-4.5/Opus 4.6 and an even bigger bump with mythos-preview.
items.zh: 我认为当它足够好到可以编码时有一个中等的提升，随着 Opus-4.5/Opus 4.6 有一个大的提升，而随着 mythos-preview 有更大的提升。

items.en: B: It is hard to see how I am not being 3x more productive. I feel like I have postdocs and grad students, and we are working towards a larger project. I think the simplest explanation is Claude—just from my individual perspective that feels sensible.
items.zh: B：很难说我现在的效率没有提高 3 倍。我感觉自己有了博士后和研究生，我们正在朝着一个更大的项目努力。我认为最简单的解释是 Claude——仅从我个人角度来看，这是合理的。

items.en: B is talking about personally being more productive, where yes I presume 3x is a floor. Then there is A who is talking explicitly about years of progress.
items.zh: B 谈论的是个人效率的提高，是的，我推测 3 倍是下限。然后 A 明确谈论的是多年的进展。

items.en: The consensus is that uplift was not that big before Opus 4.5, then Mythos Preview sent it into overdrive, and other improvements from public models were incremental. There were some voices for Model 2 or Model 4 as additional large jumps.
items.zh: 共识是，在 Opus 4.5 之前提升并没有那么大，然后 Mythos Preview 使其进入超速状态，而公共模型的其他改进则是渐进的。有一些声音认为 Model 2 或 Model 4 是额外的大跳跃。

items.en: C: this is probably the biggest factor imo. When people present experiments, they most often just point to an [agent scaffold] thread. Experimentation overhead is driven towards zero super fast.
items.zh: C：我认为这可能是最大的因素。当人们展示实验时，他们最常只是指向一个 [agent scaffold] 线程。实验开销正被极快地推向零。

items.en: D: It is just much easier to [perform] lots of [redacted] experiments that would have taken days. People don’t try [redacted] things bc it takes 1-2 days to implement per idea, but now its ~free with mythos-preview
items.zh: D：执行大量 [已编辑] 实验变得容易多了，这些实验原本需要数天。人们不会尝试 [已编辑] 的事情，因为每个想法需要 1-2 天来实现，但现在用 mythos-preview 几乎免费。

items.en: I personally think this is a large lift and has led to me trying far more ideas.
items.zh: 我个人认为这是一项很大的工程，也促使我尝试了多得多的想法。

items.en: E: I do genuinely think Claude (Claude Code, [agent-scaffold]) has been fairly significant. I've seen us discovering very promising directions ~entirely because people can spam 10 ideas at [agent-scaffold] and see what sticks.
items.zh: E：我确实认为 Claude（Claude Code，[agent-scaffold]）起到了相当重要的作用。我看到我们之所以能发现非常有前景的方向，几乎完全是因为人们可以往 [agent-scaffold] 里大量抛入 10 个想法，然后看哪些能站得住脚。

items.en: A lot of [redacted] research work is just implementation, babysitting, etc. Opus-4.5 in Claude Code is already pretty helpful with this, even if it mostly can't do end to end.
items.zh: 很多 [redacted] 的研究工作其实只是实现、照看等。Claude Code 里的 Opus-4.5 在这方面已经相当有帮助，尽管它大多无法端到端完成。

items.en: The enthusiastic set have a clear idea of their jobs and how to get AI progress.
items.zh: 热情高涨的那批人对自己的工作以及如何推动 AI 进展有清晰的认识。

items.en: 1. You come up with a bunch of experiments.
items.zh: 1. 你想出一堆实验。

items.en: 3. You analyze the results and go to step 1.
items.zh: 3. 你分析结果，然后回到第 1 步。

items.en: The AIs can run the experiments, which at the limit makes the limiting factor coming up with more new experiments worth running, which Researcher E currently says are 'nearly free' but at minimum picking the highest quality ones seems like a key part of the value add of a researcher. We're not there yet, it sounds like, and certainly I feel like I am constantly coming up with good ideas for experiments. But it is close.
items.zh: AI 可以运行实验，这最终使得限制因素变成了想出更多值得运行的新实验；Researcher E 目前称这些实验“几乎免费”，但至少挑选出质量最高的实验，似乎是研究者增值的关键部分。听起来我们还没到那一步，而且我确实觉得自己一直在不断想出好的实验想法。但已经很接近了。

items.en: The other part, once you've decided what to do or while you're running the experiment, is 'implementation, babysitting, etc,' and operational excellence.
items.zh: 另一部分，一旦你决定了要做什么，或者在运行实验的过程中，就是“实现、照看等”以及卓越的运营。

items.en: A similar story is told elsewhere, only with less confidence on magnitude of change and more openness to alternative sources of improvement.
items.zh: 别处也讲述了类似的情况，只是对变化幅度的信心较低，对替代性改进来源的开放程度更高。

items.en: F: The slope change is 50-80% Claude.
items.zh: F：斜率变化是 50-80% Claude。

items.en: Change is especially notable for this manager, who can de-risk ideas with Claude enough to get someone else excited, and would not have been able to do that at all as a manager of 10 before.
items.zh: 对这位管理者而言，变化尤为显著：他能借助 Claude 把想法做到足够去风险，从而让别人也为之兴奋；而在过去，作为管理 10 人的管理者，他根本做不到这一点。

items.en: G: The inflection point matches his vibes as to what's been happening. The two biggest contributors here are Claude automation and hiring.
items.zh: G：这个拐点与他所感受到的实际情况相符。这里最大的两个推动因素是 Claude 自动化与招聘。

items.en: Claude lets researchers try many things quickly, most of which won't work.
items.zh: Claude 让研究人员能够快速尝试许多想法，其中大多数都不会成功。

items.en: H: I think it's true [that] we're now trying a lot more experiments at the same time because of claudification.
items.zh: H：我认为确实如此，由于 claudification，我们现在同时进行的实验多了很多。

items.en: J: Before Opus-4.5 -> Claude not useful for autonomous code / Opus-4.5 -> first time useful for autonomous code / mythos-preview + [agent-scaffold] -> first time useful for autonomous experiment
items.zh: J：在 Opus-4.5 之前 -> Claude 对自主代码没有用 / Opus-4.5 -> 首次对自主代码有用 / mythos-preview + [agent-scaffold] -> 首次对自主实验有用

items.en: K thinks it was hiring. If it was hiring, we should be able to identify that based on either finding particular superstars or looking at a graph of hiring, and from what I can tell we have neither.
items.zh: K 认为这是招聘造成的。如果是招聘造成的，我们应该能够通过找到特定的超级明星或查看招聘图表来识别这一点，而据我所知，我们两者都没有。

items.en: L thinks it was [redacted] while thinking Opus 4.5 couldn’t write code, with inflection points at Mythos Preview and the mysterious Model 2. Even then this is talking price.
items.zh: L 认为这是 [已编辑] 造成的，同时认为 Opus 4.5 无法编写代码，转折点出现在 Mythos Preview 和神秘的 Model 2 上。即便如此，这谈论的是价格。

items.en: K: IMO [hiring is] probably the biggest reason …
items.zh: K：在我看来，[招聘] 可能是最大的原因……

items.en: L: Guesses 15-20% is due to AI. Don’t believe in self-reported productivity increase.
items.zh: L：猜测 15-20% 是由于 AI。不相信自我报告的生产力提升。

items.en: My favored interpretation: [redacted non-AI factor]
items.zh: 我偏好的解释：[已编辑的非 AI 因素]

items.en: (1) opus45 couldn't write code; (2) opus46 could write a little; (3) Mythos Preview a sharp inflection; (4) Model 2 is another really large improvement in how useful these things are.
items.zh: (1) opus45 无法编写代码；(2) opus46 能写一点；(3) Mythos Preview 是一个急剧的拐点；(4) Model 2 在这些东西的实用性上又是一次非常大的提升。

items.en: definitely the case that we're accelerated by claude .. Even though this rate of progress by end of year will be even faster … my attribution [mostly not to Claude] and uncertainty remain.
items.zh: 确实如此，我们被 claude 加速了……尽管到年底这一进展速度还会更快……我的归因[主要不归于 Claude]和不确定性依然存在。

items.en: One impact is SWE acceleration, which is extremely substantial. We're definitely benefiting from that differentially between 2025 and 2026.
items.zh: 一个影响是 SWE 加速，这极其显著。我们确实在 2025 到 2026 年间从中获得了差异化收益。

full.sec: This Infinite Series Likely Has a Finite Sum
full.secZh: 这个无穷级数可能有一个有限和

paras.en: If we follow the natural implications of the trend lines we see, each stage is sufficiently faster than the previous stage that you finish an unlimited number of steps in a finite time, plausibly as soon as next year, also known as a singularity. The report found no clear bottlenecks blocking that from happening in the next 12 months.
paras.zh: 如果我们遵循所见趋势线的自然推论，每个阶段都比前一阶段快得多，以至于你可以在有限时间内完成无限多个步骤，很可能就在明年，也就是所谓的奇点。报告没有发现明显的瓶颈阻碍这在未来 12 个月内发生。

paras.en: Whether or not this goes fully vertical depends on various factors, such as the change in the diminishing returns rate, compute-labor substitutability and the true pace of acceleration, and the shape of the future tech tree and implications of physics. It could go either way.
paras.zh: 这是否会完全垂直发展取决于多种因素，例如边际回报递减率的变化、算力与劳动力的可替代性以及加速的真实速度，还有未来技术树的形状和物理学的约束。两种可能都存在。

paras.en: I don't think full RSI and passing the relevant points of no return is a favorite to happen in 2027, but at this point I would no longer be surprised if that happened.
paras.zh: 我不认为完全递归自我改进（RSI）并越过相关不可逆转点会在 2027 年成为最可能发生的事，但事到如今，如果那真的发生了，我也不会再感到惊讶。

paras.en: Ajeya Cotra (METR): If we take it at face value that AI is now nearly doubling the rate of AI capabilities progress and assume acceleration from AI is smooth, this naively implies that we would reach extreme superintelligence within a year.
paras.zh: Ajeya Cotra（METR）：如果我们按字面理解，即 AI 现在几乎使 AI 能力进步的速度翻倍，并假设来自 AI 的加速是平滑的，这朴素地意味着我们将在一年内达到极端的超级智能。

full.sec: We Cannot Say What We Cannot Say
full.secZh: 我们无法说出我们无法说出的话

paras.en: Throughout, METR had to consider Anthropic's ability to pull access for this or future projects, and its need to negotiate with and get cooperation from other labs. They are warning us that they may have had to make invisible compromises.
paras.zh: 在整个过程中，METR 不得不考虑 Anthropic 撤销本项目或未来项目访问权限的能力，以及自身与其他实验室谈判并争取合作的需要。他们是在提醒我们，他们可能不得不做出一些不可见的妥协。

paras.en: My presumption is that this pushes METR in the direction of underreporting potential acceleration and danger, rather than the other way around.
paras.zh: 我的推测是，这会促使 METR 倾向于低报潜在的加速与危险，而不是相反。

full.sec: Study of Anthropic’s Compute Allocation Was Postponed
full.secZh: Anthropic 算力分配研究被推迟

paras.en: Initially this study was also going to analyze Anthropic's compute allocation, but this was at least postponed, allegedly due to concerns about focus. Another obvious hypothesis is that Anthropic realized this information was rather sensitive.
paras.zh: 最初，这项研究还计划分析 Anthropic 的算力分配，但至少这一部分被推迟了，据称是出于对研究重点的顾虑。另一个显而易见的假设是，Anthropic 意识到这一信息相当敏感。

paras.en: We do not have a timeline for when we can expect this information.
paras.zh: 我们无法预计何时能获得这一信息。

paras.en: As usual, dangling something like that and then taking it away upsets people. Knowing the compute allocation is important, because it plays directly into governance proposals that attempt to pace the frontier via compute allocation.
paras.zh: 一如既往，先抛出这样的承诺、随后又将其收回，会让人不满。了解算力分配很重要，因为它直接关系到那些试图通过算力分配来调控前沿发展节奏的治理提案。

paras.en: Remember that Anthropic's September 17 post called compute 'among the most verifiable inputs to the AI R&D process' and identified it as a potential key lever for future pacing, and that it has self-reported such allocations in the past.
paras.zh: 请记住，Anthropic 在 9 月 17 日的文章中称算力是“AI 研发过程中最可验证的投入之一”，并将其确定为未来调控节奏的一个潜在关键杠杆，而且它过去曾自行报告过此类分配情况。

paras.en: I urge Anthropic to allow this part of the report to proceed. If they do not, it is hard not to interpret this as Anthropic not wanting to take compute allocation restrictions seriously as a policy mechanism.
paras.zh: 我敦促 Anthropic 允许报告的这部分内容继续推进。如果他们不这样做，就很难不将其解读为：Anthropic 并不想把算力分配限制作为一种政策机制认真对待。

paras.en: Daniel Kokotajlo: @AnthropicAI: what the fuck? The compute allocation assessment is the thing we've been pushing for the last few months. It's very important, because it is the foundation on which pacing verification depends. "to keep the focus on risk assessment" is a non-answer, a non-excuse. Do you want to pace or not?
paras.zh: Daniel Kokotajlo：@AnthropicAI：这到底是怎么回事？算力分配评估正是我们过去几个月一直在推动的事情。它非常重要，因为它是节奏验证所依赖的基础。“为了保持对风险评估的关注”是一个非回答、非借口。你们到底想不想控制节奏？

paras.en: Anthropic has had remarkable success avoiding many kinds of leaks of information, including with one notably rare exception of its memos, despite some rather inadequate security practices like 'put everything short of the model weights on Slack.'
paras.zh: Anthropic 在避免多种信息泄露方面取得了显著成功，其中包括其备忘录这一尤为罕见的例外，尽管其安全实践相当不足，例如“把除模型权重之外的一切都放在 Slack 上”。

paras.en: The danger is that Anthropic is ending up in a maximally bad spot, where due to other security flaws we have the worst of both worlds. If the redactions do not protect information due to other security lapses, all they are doing is making us unable to properly analyze or trust the reports.
paras.zh: 危险在于，Anthropic 最终陷入了一个最糟糕的境地：由于其他安全缺陷，我们两头都落空。如果这些删节因其他安全疏漏而无法保护信息，那么它们唯一的作用就是让我们无法正确分析或信任这些报告。

paras.en: This is still far better than everyone else's strategy of 'don't have METR do a report.'
paras.zh: 这仍然远好于其他人“不让 METR 做报告”的策略。

paras.en: Nathan Calvin: One irony about Anthropic's emphasis on redactions here is that they (and the other frontier AI companies) have (by their own admission?) swiss cheese level security for ~everything other than model weights so it seems extremely likely that if China wanted to they could easily have the information redacted here (see e.g. Cathedral having access to Anthropic Slack).
paras.zh: Nathan Calvin：关于 Anthropic 在此强调删节的一个讽刺之处在于，他们（以及其他前沿 AI 公司）对除模型权重之外的几乎所有内容都只有“瑞士奶酪”级别的安全（按他们自己的承认？），因此看起来极有可能的是，如果中国想要，他们可以轻易获得这里被删节的信息（例如参见 Cathedral 能够访问 Anthropic 的 Slack）。

paras.en: In other words, I expect that the redactions are not enough to actually stop sensitive Anthropic IP from leaking in high stakes adversarial settings, but they are enough to stop good faith observers, skeptics, and governments from being as likely to believe Anthropic's claim about how imminent the risks are.
paras.zh: 换句话说，我预计这些删节不足以真正阻止敏感的 Anthropic 知识产权在高风险对抗性环境中泄露，但它们足以阻止善意观察者、怀疑者和政府那么倾向于相信 Anthropic 关于风险迫近程度的说法。

paras.en: That seems like a bad tradeoff! At least give us the descriptions of the redactions or the categories of information that informed the assessment (e.g., AI accelerating algorithmic improvements).
paras.zh: 这似乎是一个糟糕的权衡！至少应向我们提供被删节内容的描述，或为评估提供依据的信息类别（例如 AI 加速算法改进）。

paras.en: I am hesitant to criticize too hard here because, of course, the other companies didn't do a partnership with METR at all, but on the other hand, Anthropic tries to present itself as different from other companies to the point that responsible folks should be rooting for them to win even at the expense of worsening race dynamics, so it also seems appropriate to hold them to a higher standard.
paras.zh: 我不太愿意在此过于严厉地批评，因为其他公司当然根本没有与 METR 建立合作关系；但另一方面，Anthropic 试图把自己塑造成与其他公司不同的形象，以至于负责任的人应当支持它胜出，即便代价是加剧竞争态势，因此对它提出更高标准似乎也是恰当的。

paras.en: It is difficult to have a high quality discussion about a report and estimation whose major sources of justification have been redacted.
paras.zh: 对于一份主要论证来源已被涂黑的报告与估算，很难展开高质量的讨论。

paras.en: From METR's perspective, the redactions are the cost of creating the report at all. From Anthropic's perspective, this is the only way to avoid leaking key info, and that has to include some amount of glomarization around what info can be shared (e.g. you have to sometimes hide information that did not need to be hidden, to avoid the fact of redaction itself leaking too much info).
paras.zh: 从 METR 的视角看，涂黑是让这份报告得以存在所付出的代价。从 Anthropic 的视角看，这是避免泄露关键信息的唯一方式，而这必然包括对哪些信息可以共享采取一定程度的含糊其辞（glomarization，即既不确认也不否认）——例如，有时你必须隐藏那些本无需隐藏的信息，以免涂黑这一事实本身泄露过多信息。

paras.en: Did Anthropic strike the right balance? My guess is no, and they redacted too aggressively, but again it is great that the report exists at all and we take what we can get. It is tough.
paras.zh: Anthropic 是否把握好了平衡？我猜没有，他们的涂黑过于激进；但话说回来，这份报告能存在本身就很了不起，我们只能拿到多少算多少。这很难。

paras.en: Ajeya Cotra (METR): Our colleagues found that Anthropic's capabilities progress has doubled, mainly due to AI. Ryan's modeling from public info suggests the whole company's R&D would be going 4-5x faster. Labor uplift would be higher still. This is a major update to very short timelines.
paras.zh: Ajeya Cotra（METR）：我们的同事发现，Anthropic 的能力进展已经翻倍，主要归功于 AI。Ryan 基于公开信息所做的建模表明，整个公司的研发速度将提升 4–5 倍。劳动力提升还会更高。这是对极短时间线的一次重大更新。

paras.en: I am sad that so much of the underlying evidence in this report was redacted. I think evidence transparency is very important for the world to figure this out in time.
paras.zh: 我很遗憾这份报告中如此多的底层证据被涂黑。我认为证据透明度对于世界及时弄清这一问题非常重要。

paras.en: Seán Ó hÉigeartaigh: I have a great deal of trust in the quality and rigor of METR's analysis, which means that their conclusion alarms me.
paras.zh: Seán Ó hÉigeartaigh：我对 METR 分析的质量与严谨性抱有极大的信任，这意味着他们的结论令我感到警觉。

paras.en: But as a member of a scientific body tasked with informing policymakers (and yes, they are interested in this topic), it is difficult to convey how frustrating it is to have to perform our role without being able to point to the actual evidence, or even confirm that we have seen and analysed it ourselves. I trust the METR team. But it's not a good epistemic situation when the ask is for decision-makers to put their trust in my trust of the METR team.
paras.zh: 但作为一家肩负为政策制定者提供信息之责的科研机构成员（是的，他们对这一议题确实感兴趣），很难表达这种挫败感：我们履行自己的职责，却无法指出实际证据，甚至无法确认我们自己已经看到并分析过这些证据。我信任 METR 团队。但当要求决策者去信任我对 METR 团队的信任时，这并不是一种良好的认知处境。

paras.en: Ryan Greenblatt is in an even tougher position, since his role relies on trust that he can keep confidential information confidential, and there have been accusations (which he vehemently denies, and which I believe are untrue) that he did leak info.
paras.zh: Ryan Greenblatt 的处境更为艰难，因为他的角色依赖于这样一种信任：他能够对机密信息保密；而且一直存在指控（他对此坚决否认，我也认为这些指控不实），称他确实泄露了信息。

paras.en: Ryan is working only from the public report in this first section, finding it to be a major update versus his expectations for 2026, although it is not clear that he had not already updated those expectations.
paras.zh: 在这一节中，Ryan 仅依据公开报告展开工作，认为相对于他对 2026 年的预期，这是一次重大更新，尽管尚不清楚他此前是否已经更新过那些预期。

paras.en: Ryan Greenblatt (METR): This report on AI R&D automation (RSI) is a big update towards ASI within 1-2 years. It says AI progress is sped up by RSI right now by around 2x. In AI 2027, this happens around March 2027.
paras.zh: Ryan Greenblatt（METR）：这份关于 AI 研发自动化（RSI）的报告，是朝 1–2 年内实现 ASI 迈出的一次重大更新。报告称，目前 RSI 使 AI 进展加速约 2 倍。在《AI 2027》中，这大约发生在 2027 年 3 月。

paras.en: I was seriously wrong about RSI speed up; I previously expected much less in 2026 (around 1.15x-1.3x). It seems as though there was specific privately available evidence that would have changed my mind.
paras.zh: 关于递归自我改进（RSI）的加速，我此前严重判断错误；我之前预计 2026 年的加速幅度要小得多（大约 1.15 倍至 1.3 倍）。似乎存在特定的私下可得的证据，本可以改变我的看法。

paras.en: I haven’t seen an unredacted version of this report; this is purely about the public report. Because so much of the underlying evidence was redacted from the public report, I think conclusions about things other than the observed 2x faster rate of progress on benchmarks depend significantly on trust for the authors of the report. (E.g., conclusions about whether this speed up is from RSI depend on trust.) I do trust the authors of the report a lot to be careful and rigorous and generally do a good job. (Note that I also work at METR.)
paras.zh: 我尚未看到这份报告的未删节版本；这里纯粹是针对公开报告而言。由于公开报告中大量底层证据被删节，我认为，对于除基准测试上观察到的 2 倍加速之外的其他结论，很大程度上取决于对报告作者的信任。（例如，关于这种加速是否源于 RSI 的结论就依赖于信任。）我非常信任报告作者会保持谨慎和严谨，并且总体上做得很好。（注：我也在 METR 工作。）

paras.en: Less extensive redactions would greatly reduce this need for trust.
paras.zh: 如果删节不那么广泛，将大大减少这种对信任的需求。

paras.en: What is Ryan’s new view? He concluded that is something he cannot share, and instead must do his best to only use information available to the public, including his own prior statements.
paras.zh: Ryan 的新观点是什么？他得出结论，这是他无法分享的，因此必须尽力只使用公开可用的信息，包括他自己先前的陈述。

paras.en: He does have to do some form of this. Glomarization is hard.
paras.zh: 他确实必须做某种形式的这件事。Glomarization（格洛玛化）很难。

paras.en: Since in my current role I may have access to other confidential information that could be relevant to timelines one way or another, **I unfortunately cannot state my all-things-considered views on ASI timelines or the probability of a software intelligence explosion right now**. Here, I’ve done some analysis of the implications using my previous public statements.
paras.zh: 由于我目前的职位可能使我接触到其他机密信息，这些信息可能以某种方式与时间线相关，**遗憾的是，我现在无法就 ASI 时间线或软件智能爆炸的概率陈述我全面考虑后的观点**。在此，我利用我之前的公开声明对影响进行了一些分析。

paras.en: A 2x acceleration in overall AI progress from RSI corresponds to a much larger than 2x RSI speed up for AI software R&D (algorithms and data); I did an estimate using my public preexisting modeling of drivers of AI progress and the public report which yielded a very rough estimate of 4.5x for how much RSI is currently accelerating AI software progress (relative to no AI automation). In the AI 2027 scenario, this much acceleration happens around March 2027.
paras.zh: RSI 带来的整体 AI 进展加速 2 倍，对应 AI 软件研发（算法和数据）的 RSI 加速远大于 2 倍；我利用我公开的现有 AI 进展驱动因素模型和公开报告进行了估算，得出了一个非常粗略的估计：目前 RSI 加速 AI 软件进展的程度为 4.5 倍（相对于没有 AI 自动化的情况）。在 AI 2027 情景中，这种程度的加速发生在 2027 年 3 月左右。

paras.en: Here are the worked details of this estimate based on my public modeling. There are two main reasons RSI speed up of AI software R&D must be larger:
paras.zh: 以下是我基于公开模型对该估计的详细计算。AI 软件研发的 RSI 加速必须更大的两个主要原因：

paras.en: - Not all of AI progress is from better software (some is from scaling up compute in training runs). I’ve previously speculated that around 2/3 of AI progress is from software improvements which implies that 2x overall AI progress acceleration requires 3x faster software progress.
paras.zh: - 并非所有 AI 进展都来自更好的软件（部分来自训练运行中算力的扩大）。我之前推测，大约 2/3 的 AI 进展来自软件改进，这意味着整体 AI 进展加速 2 倍需要软件进展加速 3 倍。

paras.en: - Diminishing returns: A fixed amount of progress requires more work over time, so to ongoingly maintain 3x faster software progress via AI automation, you need increasingly large speed boosts from AI automation (as in, speed ups relative to how fast software R&D would go without AI automation). Based on this report, it seems that there is a substantial amount of additional AI progress from automation that has occurred.
paras.zh: - 收益递减：固定数量的进展随着时间的推移需要更多的工作，因此要通过 AI 自动化持续保持 3 倍快的软件进展，你需要来自 AI 自动化的越来越大的速度提升（即相对于没有 AI 自动化时软件研发速度的加速）。根据这份报告，似乎已经发生了大量来自自动化的额外 AI 进展。

paras.en: We can estimate the effects of diminishing returns by first determining how many additional years of software progress we’ve seen (relative to the preexisting trend) and then estimating how much software R&D would slow down after a year of software progress if you held inputs fixed due to diminishing returns. I’ve previously estimated software R&D would slow down by around 2x for each year of software progress if you held inputs fixed and based on the report, it seems as though we’ve perhaps seen roughly 0.35-1.0 years of additional software progress incorporated into trained models so far (geometric mean of ~0.6).
paras.zh: 我们可以通过以下方式估计收益递减的影响：首先确定我们观察到了多少额外的软件进步年数（相对于已有的趋势），然后估计在投入固定的情况下，由于收益递减，软件研发在一年软件进步后会放缓多少。我之前估计，在投入固定的情况下，软件研发每取得一年的软件进步，就会放缓约 2 倍。根据报告，到目前为止，我们可能已经看到大约 0.35-1.0 年的额外软件进步被纳入训练模型（几何平均约 0.6）。

paras.en: This combines to \(3 * 2^{\sim 0.6} = \sim 4.5\). (Relevant public modeling and numbers I’m using [here] and [here].
paras.zh: 这综合起来是 \(3 * 2^{\sim 0.6} = \sim 4.5\)。（我使用的相关公开建模和数字见[这里]和[这里]。

paras.en: Alexander Berger (Quoting Ryan): “Since ... I may have access to other confidential information that could be relevant to timelines one way or another, I unfortunately cannot state my all-things-considered views on ASI timelines or the probability of a software intelligence explosion right now”
paras.zh: Alexander Berger（引用 Ryan）：“由于……我可能接触到其他机密信息，这些信息可能以某种方式与时间线相关，不幸的是，我现在无法就 ASI 时间线或软件智能爆炸的概率陈述我全面考虑后的观点。”

paras.en: roon (OpenAI): I think he should state his all things considered views on ASI timelines. it seems implausible that that leaks any bits of info on training IP
paras.zh: roon（OpenAI）：我认为他应该就 ASI 时间线陈述他全面考虑后的观点。这似乎不太可能泄露任何关于训练知识产权的信息。

paras.en: Nathan Calvin: yeah, lab employees already vaguely talk about short timelines from private info frequently. If Ryan isn't doing it because he thinks the cos would be mad they should explicitly make clear that its fine for him to do it (and I agree its silly for them to be mad about that.)
paras.zh: Nathan Calvin：是的，实验室员工已经经常从私人信息中模糊地谈论短时间线。如果 Ryan 不这样做是因为他认为公司会生气，他们应该明确表示他这样做没问题（我也同意他们为此生气是愚蠢的。）

paras.en: Daniel Kokotajlo: Totally agree. I think METR is being persnickety to the point of self-sabotage here, going way beyond normal confidentiality norms.
paras.zh: Daniel Kokotajlo：完全同意。我认为 METR 在这里过于吹毛求疵，甚至到了自我破坏的程度，远远超出了正常的保密规范。

paras.en: In this case, I believe the vast majority of the unnecessary secrecy is due to Anthropic. That can include 'Anthropic created ambiguity on necessary secrecy levels.'
paras.zh: 在这种情况下，我认为绝大部分不必要的保密都源于 Anthropic。这可以包括“Anthropic 在必要保密级别上制造了模糊性”。

paras.en: Back in the 2010s, in order to avoid potentially sharing insights that advanced capabilities, MIRI (where Jessica Taylor once worked) had an extreme amount of secrecy, including within MIRI, in ways that in hindsight were highly counterproductive. Knowing what we know now, the warnings that AI was dangerous were themselves far more dangerous than any technical knowledge.
paras.zh: 早在 2010 年代，为了避免可能分享会提升能力水平的洞见，MIRI（Jessica Taylor 曾在那里工作）实行了极端的保密措施，包括在 MIRI 内部也是如此，事后看来这种做法极具反效果。以我们现在的认知来看，关于 AI 危险的警告本身，远比任何技术知识都更危险。

paras.en: Reading something like the above raises the question of whether we are making that mistake once again. It certainly seems bizarre to hold back overall timeline conclusions. Would that really leak sensitive information?
paras.zh: 读到上面这样的内容，会让人质疑我们是否正在重蹈覆辙。对整体时间线结论秘而不宣，确实显得很奇怪。那真的会泄露敏感信息吗？

paras.en: Jessica Taylor: MIRI glomarizing & secrecy culture has spread to other AI safety orgs.
paras.zh: Jessica Taylor：MIRI 的 glomar 式回避与保密文化已经蔓延到了其他 AI 安全组织。

paras.en: Kelsey Piper: entirely wrong diagnosis IMO: Greenblatt was alleged in the WSJ to have leaked secrets to The Information (almost certainly false), which would make a lot of people more cautious about saying things people might take as a leak.
paras.zh: Kelsey Piper：我认为这完全是错误的诊断：据《华尔街日报》报道，Greenblatt 被指控向 The Information 泄露机密（几乎肯定是假的），这会让很多人在说话时更加谨慎，以免被人当作泄密。

paras.en: Jessica Taylor: This is a good point for Ryan specifically, and if it were just Ryan doing this, there would be less justification for this diagnosis; however, there are other signs here.
paras.zh: Jessica Taylor：这对 Ryan 个人来说是个很好的观点，如果只是 Ryan 这样做，这个诊断的理由就不那么充分；然而，这里还有其他迹象。

paras.en: Bubbling Creek: I really do not think METR is the one pushing for this level of secrecy; it's Anthropic.
paras.zh: Bubbling Creek：我真的不认为 METR 是推动这种保密程度的一方，是 Anthropic。

paras.en: Jessica Taylor: Yeah, good point, this seems more Anthropic than METR. Anthropic is relatively secretive for an AI company.
paras.zh: Jessica Taylor：是的，说得好，这看起来更像是 Anthropic 而不是 METR。对于一家 AI 公司来说，Anthropic 相对比较保密。

full.sec: Review of the Risk Report from August 2026
full.secZh: 对 2026 年 8 月风险报告的评述

items.en: **Along with the main report, METR also** reviewed the August 2026 Anthropic Risk Report, which in turn covered events up to July 15. That seems so quaint now.
items.zh: **除主报告之外，METR 还**评述了 2026 年 8 月的 Anthropic 风险报告，该报告涵盖的事件截至 7 月 15 日。如今看来，这已显得颇为天真。

items.en: The central claim of that risk report is that at the time there was low risk of directly automating R&D in key domains. Key reasoning for this was redacted from the public version. METR got to look at the private version.
items.zh: 该风险报告的核心主张是：当时在关键领域直接自动化研发（R&D）的风险较低。其关键推理在公开版本中被删节。METR 得以查看非公开版本。

items.en: METR's conclusion is that the line probably was not crossed, but that confidence that we had not seen 2x acceleration by that point is not high, and that the report understated the level of acceleration present.
items.zh: METR 的结论是：这条线很可能并未被越过，但对于“截至当时尚未出现 2 倍加速”这一判断的信心并不高，且该报告低估了实际存在的加速程度。

items.en: The report basically sold us the 'Mythos-class models were a step change and rates of acceleration are otherwise not so high' model, in ways that were somewhat misleading, and in ways that do not seem to reflect Anthropic's private information.
items.zh: 该报告基本上向我们推销了“Mythos 级模型是一次阶跃式变化，而其他方面的加速率并不那么高”这一模型，其方式在某种程度上具有误导性，且似乎并未反映 Anthropic 的私有信息。

items.en: I am pretty not happy about this one. The threshold was 2, they reported the answer was 'less than 2' and it turned out the answer was 1.97, well within any reasonable margin of error, and also known as 'approximately 2', with METR's error bounds being something like [1.3, 2.8]:
items.zh: 我对这件事相当不满。阈值是 2，他们报告的结果是“小于 2”，而实际结果是 1.97，完全落在任何合理的误差范围内，也可称为“约等于 2”，而 METR 的误差范围大致为 [1.3, 2.8]：

items.en: METR: We believe a reader of the public report would interpret the phrase "less than a factor of 2" to imply an estimate meaningfully below 2; thus it is surprising that the private risk report's figures imply 1.97. A better description would seem to be "around 2."
items.zh: METR：我们认为，公开报告的读者会将“小于 2 倍”这一表述理解为估计值明显低于 2；因此，令人意外的是，非公开风险报告中的数字却意味着 1.97。更恰当的描述似乎是“约为 2 倍”。

items.en: Claim 2 (Private Risk Report): Overall we expect that end-to-end growth in [redacted] is slightly less than twice as fast as it would be without AI assistance.
items.zh: 主张 2（非公开风险报告）：总体而言，我们预计在[已隐去]中的端到端增长比没有 AI 辅助时略快不到两倍。

items.capEn: This creates a wording ratchet going forward. If I see ‘less than a factor of [X]’ I will assume that simply means that the point estimate is some amount less than [X], but that it could be very close to [X], and [X] could easily be within the margin of error. Going forward, if they want to communicate ‘no seriously this is not close to [X]’ they will have to say that it is not close.
items.capZh: 这创造了一种措辞棘轮效应。如果我看到‘小于 [X] 倍’，我会假设这仅仅意味着点估计值小于 [X] 某个量，但可能非常接近 [X]，而 [X] 很容易在误差范围内。今后，如果他们想传达‘不，说真的，这并不接近 [X]’，他们必须说它不接近。

items.capEn: Redacting information is fine, but the public version is framed to imply little progress, where the private verison is framed to imply expectations of more progress. The whole point of the risk report is to share exactly this intuition. Not cool.
items.capZh: 涂黑信息没问题，但公开版本的框架暗示进展甚微，而私人版本的框架暗示预期更多进展。风险报告的全部意义就是分享这种直觉。不酷。

paras.en: Here is Anthropic cofounder Sam McCandlish's take on the report. He agrees with many of its conclusions, and admits that a lot of information was redacted to avoid giving competitors a roadmap to go faster.
paras.zh: 以下是 Anthropic 联合创始人 Sam McCandlish 对这份报告的看法。他同意其中的许多结论，并承认大量信息被删减，以避免给竞争对手提供加速发展的路线图。

paras.en: Sam McCandlish (Cofounder, Anthropic): I'm Sam, one of Anthropic's co-founders, and I lead much of our safety work. I'm going to have more to share on that work over the coming months.
paras.zh: Sam McCandlish（Anthropic 联合创始人）：我是 Sam，Anthropic 的联合创始人之一，负责领导我们的大部分安全研究工作。在接下来的几个月里，我将分享更多关于这项工作的内容。

paras.en: I thought I'd start by sharing a few thoughts on the latest report from @METR_Evals.
paras.zh: 我想先分享一些关于 @METR_Evals 最新报告的想法。

paras.en: The speed of progress in model capabilities is one of the most important questions in AI safety, and METR's work here provides the public with an independent, external view into how this is happening inside Anthropic. I'll talk more about some of the details below, but first some context for those new to this work.
paras.zh: 模型能力进步的速度是 AI 安全中最重要的问题之一，METR 的工作为公众提供了一个独立的外部视角，来了解 Anthropic 内部是如何发生这种进步的。我将在下面详细讨论一些细节，但首先为不熟悉这项工作的人提供一些背景。

paras.en: How quickly AI progress is accelerating has many important safety implications, since it determines how quickly the risks from advanced models increase. But, because most research happens within the frontier labs, it's difficult for external observers and policy makers to get a strong sense of what that rate is. We kicked off the process with METR that led to this report earlier in the year, in anticipation of progress continuing to accelerate.
paras.zh: AI 进步加速的速度有多快，具有许多重要的安全影响，因为它决定了先进模型带来的风险增加的速度。但是，由于大多数研究发生在前沿实验室内部，外部观察者和政策制定者很难对其速度有强烈的感知。今年早些时候，我们启动了与 METR 的合作流程，最终促成了这份报告，因为我们预计进步将继续加速。

paras.en: For this report, we gave METR access to a range of sensitive internal data, including benchmark scores for unreleased models, estimates of how models are progressing, and interviews with our researchers. They had complete independence to form their own conclusions.
paras.zh: 为了这份报告，我们让 METR 访问了一系列敏感的内部数据，包括未发布模型的基准测试分数、模型进展的估计，以及对我们研究人员的访谈。他们拥有完全的独立性来形成自己的结论。

paras.en: Many of their conclusions match my own. AI is speeding up our research, but it's hard to say exactly how much. While they conclude AI can't yet make the most important contributions to model training on its own, they think the pace of development could, by default, accelerate further.
paras.zh: 他们的许多结论与我自己的结论一致。AI 正在加速我们的研究，但很难确切地说加速了多少。尽管他们得出结论，AI 尚不能独自对模型训练做出最重要的贡献，但他们认为，发展速度可能会默认进一步加快。

paras.en: This work began well before and is separate from the embedded third-party evaluators that are part of our commitment to pacing the frontier, but it's a good illustration of why we think evaluators are a good idea. The more access reviewers have, the clearer a picture they can form of the situation and the better-positioned they are to highlight situations like this one.
paras.zh: 这项工作早在嵌入的第三方评估者之前就已开始，并且与后者是分开的，后者是我们对前沿模型进行节奏控制承诺的一部分。但这项工作很好地说明了为什么我们认为评估者是一个好主意。评审者获得的访问权限越多，他们就能对情况形成更清晰的了解，也更有能力突出像这样的情况。

paras.en: We redacted a lot, and I accept that this makes it harder for others to check METR's work. But we determined that sharing exactly what is driving the speedup isn't the right thing to do, both because it's commercially sensitive and because it risks handing out a roadmap for others to go faster. That would make the risks METR is worried about worse. That's a tradeoff. I think we made the right call, though we're continuing to assess the pros and cons here.
paras.zh: 我们做了大量删节，我承认这会让其他人更难核查 METR 的工作。但我们认定，分享究竟是什么在推动加速并不合适，这既因为涉及商业敏感性，也因为有可能为其他人提供加速的路线图。那会使 METR 所担心的风险变得更糟。这是一个权衡。我认为我们做出了正确的决定，尽管我们仍在继续评估这里的利弊。

paras.en: In the coming weeks, we plan to share a report with our own analysis of the speed of AI progress within Anthropic, including where we stand against our Responsible Scaling Policy, plus new steps we're taking to strengthen our safety and security practices as AI keeps improving quickly.
paras.zh: 在接下来的几周里，我们计划分享一份报告，其中包含我们自己对 Anthropic 内部 AI 进展速度的分析，包括我们在 Responsible Scaling Policy 方面的立场，以及随着 AI 持续快速改进，我们为加强安全与安保实践所采取的新步骤。

paras.en: Daniel Kokotajlo: It is pretty rich of you to cite "others could go faster" as a reason to redact so much important information when you yourself do not appear to be slowing down much at all. Nor are you throwing yourself behind efforts to pace the frontier with nearly the gusto that you would if it was your top priority. Not to mention "commercial sensitivity"—you yourself have said human extinction is a plausible outcome; why are you even talking about commercial factors? (Well, I guess honesty is good, and since it IS apparently a factor in your decision...)
paras.zh: Daniel Kokotajlo：你引用“其他人可能进展更快”作为删减如此多重要信息的理由，这真是相当讽刺，因为你自己似乎根本没有放慢多少。你也没有像如果这是你的首要任务那样，全力投入到为前沿模型定速的努力中。更不用说“商业敏感性”了——你自己说过人类灭绝是一个可能的结果，为什么你还在谈论商业因素？（好吧，我想诚实是好事，而且既然这显然是你们决策中的一个因素……）

paras.en: To all my friends at Anthropic: Your company appears to be recklessly gambling with our lives. You fancy yourselves the more responsible alternative to OpenAI (as they fancied themselves compared to Google), but judging by actions rather than words, the similarities between the three of you seem stronger than the differences.
paras.zh: 致我在 Anthropic 的所有朋友：你们的公司似乎在鲁莽地拿我们的生命赌博。你们自认为是比 OpenAI 更负责任的替代选择（就像他们自认为比 Google 更负责任一样），但根据行动而非言辞来判断，你们三者之间的相似之处似乎比差异更强烈。

paras.en: Some of the redactions can be justified as avoiding giving competitors a roadmap, but I do not see how the full extent of the redactions can be justified that way. Time estimates for future acceleration by both METR in general and Ryan Greenblatt in particular are being redacted. How would those numbers provide a roadmap?
paras.zh: 一些删减可以解释为避免给竞争对手提供路线图，但我看不出全部删减如何能以这种方式被合理化。METR 整体以及 Ryan Greenblatt 个人对未来加速的时间估计正在被删减。这些数字怎么会提供路线图呢？

paras.en: More importantly, you believe all this is accurate, and you intend to keep going?
paras.zh: 更重要的是，你相信这一切都是准确的，并且你打算继续下去？

paras.en: We also still have data points like this:
paras.zh: 我们仍然有这样的数据点：

paras.en: Theo Bearman: ANTHROPIC'S RESPONSIBLE SCALING OFFICER: "In the coming weeks, we plan to share a report with our own analysis of the speed of AI progress within Anthropic, including where we stand against our Responsible Scaling Policy, plus new steps we're taking to strengthen our safety and security practices as AI keeps improving quickly."
paras.zh: Theo Bearman：Anthropic 的负责任 Scaling（规模扩张）官：“在接下来的几周内，我们计划分享一份报告，其中包含我们自己对 Anthropic 内部 AI 进展速度的分析，包括我们在负责任 Scaling 政策方面的现状，以及随着 AI 持续快速改进，我们为加强安全与安保实践所采取的新措施。”

paras.en: Nathan Calvin: If Anthropic wants me to think these steps are real/credible, they should put it in their SB 53/RAISE Act Frontier Compliance Framework.
paras.zh: Nathan Calvin：如果 Anthropic 想让我认为这些措施是真实/可信的，他们就应该把它写进其 SB 53/RAISE Act 前沿合规框架中。

paras.en: State law gave Anthropic and OpenAI a mechanism for making credible statements about their behavior, and they mostly choose not to use it on the risks they are most worried about (neither company includes anything in their compliance frameworks about internal deployment RSI risk, though Anthropic says maybe at some point in the future they will. Now seems like as good a time as any???!!!???)
paras.zh: 州法律为 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 提供了一种就其行为做出可信声明的机制，而他们大多选择不在自己最担心的风险上使用它（两家公司的合规框架中都没有提及内部部署 RSI 风险，尽管 Anthropic 表示未来某个时候可能会提及。现在似乎正是最好的时机？？？！！！？？？）

paras.en: Peter Wildeford: This is pretty much how things have gone...
paras.zh: Peter Wildeford：事情基本上就是这样发展的……

paras.en: ANTHROPIC: "AI is extremely perilous and should be carefully regulated"
paras.zh: ANTHROPIC：“AI 极其危险，应当受到谨慎监管”

paras.en: CALIFORNIA GOV: "Ok, we will regulate you."
paras.zh: 加州政府：“好，我们会监管你们。”

paras.en: ANTHROPIC: "No! Good regulation is really hard to get right. We know so little about what to do. Instead we should let companies carefully iterate over time."
paras.zh: Anthropic：“不！好的监管真的很难做对。我们对该做什么知之甚少。相反，我们应该让公司随着时间推移谨慎地迭代。”

paras.en: CALIFORNIA GOV: "Oh ok. How about we do a thing where you get to write what the rules are but we will hold you to them? Then you can make your own commitments as you think is best but they will be true commitments!"
paras.zh: 加州政府：“哦，好吧。那我们这样如何：由你们来写规则是什么，但我们会要求你们遵守这些规则？这样你们就可以按照自己认为最好的方式做出自己的承诺，但这些将是真正的承诺！”

paras.en: ANTHROPIC: "Nah, we'd rather make fake commitments."
paras.zh: Anthropic：“不，我们宁愿做出虚假的承诺。”
