paras.zh: 加州政府：

paras.en: Nathan Calvin: **Worth reading**. Dario says that one of the ways that Anthropic can justify remaining at the frontier (with the associated risks) is because the company is effective at pushing for strong AI regulation. I think Anthropic's track record here is more complex than he implies.
paras.zh: Nathan Calvin：**值得一读**。Dario 说，Anthropic 能够证明自己留在前沿（并承担相关风险）的正当性，其中一个理由是该公司在推动强有力的 AI 监管方面卓有成效。我认为 Anthropic 在这方面的过往记录比他暗示的要复杂得多。

paras.en: Max Winga: The lawyers here really held @DarioAmodei's feet to the fire and it's interesting to see how he squirmed under oath about AI extinction risk. Under penalty of perjury he's reaffirmed his belief that AI is the greatest threat humanity has ever faced.
paras.zh: Max Winga：这里的律师们确实让 @DarioAmodei 如坐针毡，看到他在宣誓后面对 AI 灭绝风险问题时如何坐立不安，很有意思。在作伪证受罚的约束下，他重申了自己的信念：AI 是人类有史以来面临的最大威胁。

paras.en: Peter Wildeford: Anthropic will really be like "you believe in slowing down? that pales in effectiveness to my strategy, racing so fast that we have credibility to push for strong regulation" and then not push for strong regulation
paras.zh: Peter Wildeford：Anthropic 真的会这样说：“你相信要放慢速度？那在有效性上远不如我的策略——跑得足够快，从而获得推动强监管的可信度”，然后却并不去推动强监管。

paras.en: Daniel Tan overstates a bit here, but I agree that Anthropic's actions that supposedly 'race to the top' often do not look so different from what they would do if they were instead racing to superintelligence.
paras.zh: Daniel Tan 在这里有些夸大其词，但我同意：Anthropic 那些据称是“向上竞争”的行为，往往看起来与它们如果是在奔向超级智能时会做的事并无太大区别。

full.sec: People Update Their Timelines and Expectations
full.secZh: 人们更新他们的时间线和期望

paras.en: Andrew Curran: Judging by the posts on my timeline, today is the big update on both RSI and ASI for many people in this community. I went through this in November 2022, so I know exactly how you feel. I know nobody drinks anymore, but I would suggest having a drink.
paras.zh: Andrew Curran：从我的时间线上的帖子来看，今天对这个社区的许多人来说是关于 RSI 和 ASI 的重大更新。我在 2022 年 11 月经历过这个，所以我完全知道你们的感觉。我知道现在没人喝酒了，但我建议喝一杯。

paras.en: Trevor Levin: This report and reactions from people I trust (like Jake) are making me physically ill. As far as I can tell, Anthropic's central plan is to continue this acceleration of AI capabilities until we're getting decades of AI capabilities growth in a year. Given our very limited ability to understand or control AI systems, this would be extremely reckless and completely unacceptable, and it should be the single top priority of civil society and the US government to stop them and other companies from doing this.
paras.zh: Trevor Levin：这份报告以及我信任的人（比如 Jake）的反应让我感到身体不适。据我所知，Anthropic 的核心计划是继续这种 AI 能力的加速，直到我们在一年内获得数十年的 AI 能力增长。鉴于我们理解和控制 AI 系统的能力非常有限，这将是极其鲁莽和完全不可接受的，阻止他们和其他公司这样做应该成为公民社会和美国政府的首要任务。

paras.en: Dane Sherburn (former OpenAI): I feel sick after reading today’s METR report. I’m worried for my friends and family. I don’t know what evidence people will need to see before they start taking these risks seriously.
paras.zh: Dane Sherburn（前 OpenAI）：读了今天的 METR 报告后，我感到恶心。我为我的朋友和家人担心。我不知道人们需要看到什么证据才能开始认真对待这些风险。

paras.en: If you’re undecided about helping, please act; there's many opportunities to help.
paras.zh: 如果你对是否提供帮助犹豫不决，请行动起来；有很多机会可以提供帮助。

paras.en: Samuel Albanie (Google DeepMind): recommend internalizing the implications of this METR thread.
paras.zh: Samuel Albanie（Google DeepMind）：建议内化这个 METR 线程的含义。

paras.en: (1) capabilities are speeding up significantly
paras.zh: (1) 能力正在显著加速提升

paras.en: (2) the speedup is not driven by growth in compute
paras.zh: (2) 这种加速并非由算力增长所驱动

paras.en: (METR estimates an overall speedup of approximately 2x on well-specified tasks by Oct 2026 vs. Mar 2024 to Oct 2025)
paras.zh: （METR 估计，到 2026 年 10 月，在定义明确的任务上，相较 2024 年 3 月至 2025 年 10 月，整体加速约为 2 倍）

paras.en: There are a bunch of qualifications/caveats worth reading in the thread itself.
paras.zh: 该推文串本身还包含许多值得一读的限定条件与注意事项。

paras.en: Jake Mendel (Coefficient Giving): I've always had substantially longer timelines than my friends at Anthropic — I've been concerned that they're in an echo chamber and believing the hype about their own models too much, and that they're underestimating bottlenecks and unknown unknowns. And there have definitely been specific occasions when they have overstated how much uplift they were getting from their models. Nonetheless, if METR is correct here (and I think they are among the most trustworthy sources on this topic), then my Anthropic friends have been much more right about timelines than me.
paras.zh: Jake Mendel（Coefficient Giving）：我的时间线一直比我在 Anthropic 的朋友们长得多——我一直担心他们身处回音室之中，过于相信关于自家模型的炒作，并且低估了瓶颈与未知的未知。而且确实有过一些具体场合，他们夸大了自家模型所带来的提升幅度。尽管如此，如果 METR 在这里是对的（而我认为他们是该话题上最可信的来源之一），那么我的 Anthropic 朋友们在时间线判断上比我正确得多。

paras.en: This report is also some evidence that a software-only singularity is plausible. I now think that we are more than 50% likely to have full blown superintelligence in the next 18 months, absent a slowdown. I need to call my family.
paras.zh: 这份报告也提供了一些证据，表明纯软件奇点是有可能的。我现在认为，在没有放缓的情况下，未来 18 个月内出现完全成熟的超级智能的概率超过 50%。我需要给家人打个电话。

paras.en: I think the US government should make them stop.
paras.zh: 我认为美国政府应该让他们停下来。

paras.en: If you already believed the labs that have been screaming similar things for months, and do not trust information gated by redactions, perhaps you did not update so much.
paras.zh: 如果你已经相信了那些几个月来一直大声疾呼类似事情的实验室，并且不信任经过删减的信息，那么也许你并没有更新多少。

paras.en: Dylan Bowman (Apollo Research): I have finished this report and learned approximately nothing (because of redactions) and updated a tiny tiny bit towards longer timelines.
paras.zh: Dylan Bowman（Apollo Research）：我读完了这份报告，几乎什么也没学到（因为删减），并且向更长的时间线更新了极小极小的一点。

paras.en: Tiny tiny bit towards longer timelines because of this sentence: “Anthropic’s internal benchmarks are increasingly saturated”. This sentence is about AECI evals but maybe is also true of their production evals (low conf, hence “tiny tiny”)
paras.zh: 向更长的时间线更新极小极小的一点，是因为这句话：“Anthropic 的内部基准正日益饱和”。这句话是关于 AECI 评估的，但也许也适用于他们的生产评估（置信度低，因此“极小极小”）

paras.en: I also expected more than 2x uplift. I think Apollo's internal uplift is ~1.5-2x.
paras.zh: 我也预期会有超过 2 倍的提升。我认为 Apollo 的内部提升约为 1.5–2 倍。

paras.en: The report also glosses over the biggest plausible alternative to researcher uplift driving the acceleration, which is data uplift (like RL environment pipelines and automated quality control).
paras.zh: 该报告还忽略了推动加速的、除研究者提升之外最有可能的替代解释，即数据提升（如强化学习环境流水线和自动化质量控制）。

paras.en: Peter Wildeford attributes a lot of the gains to Anthropic catching up on RL if you look only at public information, and remains skeptical that there is a full ~2x speedup happening, but trusts METR's analysis of private info.
paras.zh: Peter Wildeford 认为，如果只看公开信息，大部分收益应归因于 Anthropic 在强化学习上的追赶；他仍怀疑是否真的存在完整的约 2 倍加速，但信任 METR 对私有信息的分析。

paras.en: Peter Wildeford: The RL shift could plausibly explain much of the benchmark acceleration. RL's share grew fastest before METR's break point (4% to 24% from 2024Q1 to 2025Q3), but if you add an additional assumption for a 2-3 quarter lag from compute to released models, that lines up with a ~1.4-2.2x speedup, which is what we see. Also, I think catch-up on RL probably explains some of why Anthropic is accelerating more than other labs.
paras.zh: Peter Wildeford：强化学习的转变可能合理地解释了基准加速的很大一部分。在 METR 的断点之前，强化学习的占比增长最快（从 2024Q1 的 4% 增至 2025Q3 的 24%），但如果额外假设从算力到模型发布存在 2–3 个季度的滞后，这就与我们所看到的约 1.4–2.2 倍加速相吻合。此外，我认为强化学习上的追赶可能部分解释了为何 Anthropic 的加速超过其他实验室。

paras.en: Before Oct 2025, Anthropic's pace was below the overall frontier's. OpenAI went RL-heavy first (o1, Sep 2024) and Anthropic followed later (Claude 3.7 Sonnet, Feb 2025).
paras.zh: 在 2025 年 10 月之前，Anthropic 的节奏低于整体前沿水平。OpenAI 率先重度投入强化学习（o1，2024 年 9 月），Anthropic 随后跟进（Claude 3.7 Sonnet，2025 年 2 月）。

paras.en: So part of Anthropic's 1.9x could be a late RL ramp from a low baseline. METR flags this in the chart subtitle and I find it plausible. But the all-developer frontier still accelerated ~1.4x, so catch-up doesn't explain all of it.
paras.zh: 因此，Anthropic 的 1.9 倍加速中，有一部分可能来自后期从低基线开始的强化学习（RL）爬升。METR 在图表副标题中指出了这一点，我认为这是合理的。但所有开发者的前沿仍然加速了约 1.4 倍，所以追赶效应并不能解释全部。

paras.en: Additionally, this "RL is doing the work" makes a testable prediction, however... since RL share is plateauing (50% to 53% to 55% over the last three quarters), this means benchmark growth should slow by mid-2027. If it doesn't, something else is driving it. Worth watching. To be clear, 1.4x faster benchmark progress is very different from engineers being 1.4x faster. Per METR's report, engineers can be sped up ~12x while overall progress only speeds up ~1.4x, because of compute constraints and Amdahl's law.
paras.zh: 此外，这种“RL 在起作用”的说法做出了一个可检验的预测，然而……由于 RL 占比正在趋于平稳（过去三个季度分别为 50%、53%、55%），这意味着基准增长应在 2027 年中期放缓。如果没有，那就是其他因素在驱动。值得关注。需要明确的是，基准进展快 1.4 倍与工程师快 1.4 倍是非常不同的。根据 METR 的报告，由于算力限制和阿姆达尔定律，工程师的速度可以提高约 12 倍，而整体进展只加速约 1.4 倍。

paras.en: I should clarify that I personally believe AI is responsible for like at least 1.4x acceleration, though it sounds like this is more based on METR having private information and me trusting METR than us having clear independent public information.
paras.zh: 我应该澄清，我个人认为 AI 至少贡献了 1.4 倍的加速，尽管这听起来更多是基于 METR 拥有私有信息以及我信任 METR，而不是我们拥有清晰的独立公开信息。

paras.en: To be clearer, METR says that they have "received convincing evidence that the acceleration was not due to an acceleration in the scale of training compute" but that "further details on this evidence were redacted" and I believe METR's analysis even though it requires trusting private information and cannot be confirmed with public information.
paras.zh: 更清楚地说，METR 表示他们“收到了令人信服的证据，表明加速并非由于训练算力规模的加速”，但“关于这一证据的进一步细节被涂黑”，我相信 METR 的分析，尽管这需要信任私有信息且无法用公开信息证实。

paras.en: Even if we don’t worry about alignment, the bare minimum requirement for attempting to build a superintelligence is not to leak all your algorithmic secrets or model weights. The AI industry is not ready to meet even that bar.
paras.zh: 即使我们不考虑对齐问题，尝试构建超级智能的最低要求也是不要泄露你所有的算法秘密或模型权重。AI 行业连这一门槛都尚未准备好达到。

paras.en: We are even less prepared than that to build an aligned or inherently safe superintelligence, especially if we try to build it in 2027 or 2028.
paras.zh: 我们距离构建一个对齐的或本质安全的超级智能的准备程度还要更低，尤其是如果我们试图在 2027 或 2028 年就把它造出来的话。

paras.en: Ajeya Cotra (METR): Very strong security, both for model weights and algorithmic secrets themselves, is a minimum prerequisite for undergoing an intelligence explosion next year without running very large risks of killing billions of people.
paras.zh: Ajeya Cotra（METR）：极强的安全性——无论是模型权重还是算法秘密本身——是在明年经历智能爆炸而不冒造成数十亿人死亡的巨大风险的最低前提条件。

paras.en: Ryan Greenblatt: I recommend @ajeya_cotra's post about implications of the AI R&D report. Ajeya argues:
paras.zh: Ryan Greenblatt：我推荐 @ajeya_cotra 关于 AI 研发报告影响的帖子。Ajeya 论证道：

paras.en: - A 2x speed-up is dramatic.
paras.zh: - 2 倍加速就是巨大的。

paras.en: - 2x faster progress implies a much larger effective "time warp bubble" speed for staff.
paras.zh: - 2 倍的进展速度意味着员工的有效“时间扭曲气泡”速度要大得多。

paras.en: - This could compound extremely fast.
paras.zh: - 这可能会以极快的速度复合增长。

paras.en: - We aren't prepared.
paras.zh: - 我们还没有准备好。

full.sec: If (If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies) Then Don’t Let Anyone Build It
full.secZh: 如果（若任何人建造它，所有人都会死）那么就别让任何人建造它

items.en: At minimum, we need to know what they fully think, and that can start by having Congress read the unredacted report and decide if they believe the full report.
items.zh: 至少，我们需要知道他们到底怎么想，而这可以从让国会阅读未经删节的报告、并判断他们是否相信完整报告开始。

items.en: If they do believe the full report, they should act accordingly.
items.zh: 如果他们确实相信完整报告，就应当据此采取行动。

items.en: Kelsey Piper: Of course, the report might be wrong, and Anthropic's employees might be deluding themselves about their progress. So I want Congress to read the unredacted report. I want lawmakers to hire brilliant RSI believers and brilliant RSI skeptics, and have those experts pore over all the evidence and tell us whether these companies are experiencing some kind of mass delusion or actually reporting on an imminent disaster for humankind.
items.zh: Kelsey Piper：当然，报告可能是错的，Anthropic 的员工也可能对自己的进展自欺欺人。所以我希望国会阅读未经删节的报告。我希望立法者聘请杰出的 RSI 支持者和杰出的 RSI 怀疑者，让这些专家仔细审阅所有证据，告诉我们这些公司究竟是陷入了某种集体妄想，还是确实在报告一场迫在眉睫的人类灾难。

items.en: And if it's the latter, I want Congress to ban RSI. Make the companies demonstrate where they're spending their money, and don't let them spend it on this.
items.zh: 而如果是后者，我希望国会禁止 RSI。让这些公司证明他们的钱花在哪里，并且不许他们把钱花在这上面。

items.en: It's ridiculous for our elected representatives to be stuck reading the tea leaves from heavily redacted reports about a technology that could determine humanity's future.
items.zh: 我们选出的代表竟然只能从经过大量删节的报告中揣测一项可能决定人类未来的技术，这实在荒谬。

items.en: This is an urgent matter. Again, if we let them build it, there is a double-digit chance that by the end of 2027 it will be too late to stop it from being built, where 'it' is recursively self-improving AI that will become true superintelligence.
items.zh: 这是一件紧迫的事情。再次强调，如果我们让他们建造它，那么到 2027 年底，阻止它被建造出来就为时已晚的可能性将达到两位数百分比，这里的“它”指的是递归自我改进的 AI，它将变成真正的超级智能。

items.en: The 'don't let anyone build it' faction certainly knows how to respond to this situation.
items.zh: “不要让任何人建造它”这一派当然知道如何应对这种情况。

items.en: Congressman Greg Casar: Ban RSI.
items.zh: 国会议员 Greg Casar：禁止 RSI。

items.en: Andrew Curran: It's going to be an interesting couple of years.
items.zh: Andrew Curran：接下来几年会很有意思。

items.en: Arthur B.: Only if they ban RSI
items.zh: Arthur B.：前提是他们真的禁止 RSI。

items.en: Even Neil Chilson sees little innovation harm in ‘banning RSI’ because, by his definition, no one would be so stupid as to do it and not keep humans ‘in the loop.’
items.zh: 甚至 Neil Chilson 也认为“禁止 RSI”对创新的损害很小，因为按照他的定义，没有人会愚蠢到去做这件事却不把人类留在“循环中”。

items.en: Neil Chilson: I see little innovation harm from an RSI ban, for my definition of RSI. Little innovation harm because RSI, properly defined, is a practice too stupid to need banning. But I’m worried Alex means something different than me.
items.zh: Neil Chilson：就我所定义的 RSI 而言，我认为禁止 RSI 对创新的损害很小。损害很小，是因为正确定义下的 RSI 是一种愚蠢到无需禁止的做法。但我担心 Alex 所指的和我不同。

items.en: Daniel Filan: What's your definition of RSI?
items.zh: Daniel Filan：你对 RSI 的定义是什么？

items.en: Neil Chilson: Something like “fully relinquishing AI R&D and deployment to AI, with no ability to monitor and stop the process.”
items.zh: Neil Chilson：大致是“将 AI 研发与部署完全交给 AI，且无法监控和停止该过程”。

items.en: Which by the Sixth Law of Human Stupidity means we will definitely do it at the first opportunity if allowed to do so, also the AI companies are screaming that they are going to do it at the first opportunity if allowed to do so.
items.zh: 而根据人类愚蠢第六定律，这意味着只要被允许，我们一定会在第一时间这么做；此外，AI 公司也在叫嚣，只要被允许，他们就会在第一时间这么做。

items.en: Neil and I agree it would be deeply stupid, but for very different reasons.
items.zh: Neil 和我都认为那将是极其愚蠢的，但理由却大相径庭。

full.sec: How Can We Legally Define RSI?
full.secZh: 如何从法律上定义 RSI？

paras.en: You cannot ban that which you cannot define.
paras.zh: 你无法禁止你无法定义的东西。

paras.en: Banning an overly narrow definition, such as Neil's above, won't make us not dead.
paras.zh: 禁止一个过于狭窄的定义（例如上文 Neil 的定义），并不能让我们免于死亡。

paras.en: If you so narrowly define and ban RSI as meaning only a 100% relinquishing with zero ability to monitor, what you get is a 90% then 99% then 99.9% automated process with some illusion that you can monitor and stop the process. Then you find out you cannot stop the process and that your human is not in any of the loops that matter. Then, probably, you die.
paras.zh: 如果你把 RSI 如此狭窄地定义为仅指 100% 完全放权、且完全无法监控，并据此加以禁止，那么你得到的将是一个 90%、继而 99%、再继而 99.9% 自动化的过程，并伴有一种你能够监控并中止该过程的错觉。随后你会发现你无法中止该过程，而你的人类并不在任何真正重要的回路之中。然后，你很可能就死了。

paras.en: Legal text has to be robust to various workarounds, including in very stupid ways, as in Critch might well have a point here no matter how stupid it sounds when you say it:
paras.zh: 法律文本必须对各种规避手段具有鲁棒性，包括那些非常愚蠢的规避方式；正如 Critch 在此很可能说得有道理，无论这话说出来听起来多么愚蠢：

paras.en: Andrew Critch: This ban [on RSI] needs to be expanded to "Recursively Self-Modifying", to avoid unfortunate debates about whether killing or driving humans to extinction counts as "Improvement". (Answer: it doesn't, but many people disturbingly claim it does.)
paras.zh: Andrew Critch：这项[对 RSI 的]禁令需要扩展为“递归自我修改”（Recursively Self-Modifying），以避免关于“杀死人类或驱使人类走向灭绝是否算作‘改进’”的不幸争论。（答案：不算，但许多人令人不安地声称它算。）

paras.en: The problem with most other known definitions is that they don't work as legal text.
paras.zh: 大多数其他已知定义的问题在于，它们无法作为法律文本使用。

paras.en: Alex Bores: Every AI company is trying to fully automate AI research; to allow the AIs to build the next AI.
paras.zh: Alex Bores：每一家 AI 公司都在试图完全自动化 AI 研究；让 AI 去构建下一个 AI。

paras.en: This is called Recursive Self Improvement (RSI).
paras.zh: 这被称为递归自我改进（Recursive Self Improvement，RSI）。

paras.en: … The exact mechanism can be debated. The ban doesn't have to be permanent either (see below for both). This is not the only thing we have to do in regards to AI, far from it! But it is urgent. Congress must ban RSI.
paras.zh: ……具体机制可以讨论。禁令也不必是永久性的（关于这两点见下文）。这远不是我们在 AI 方面唯一要做的事！但它是紧迫的。国会必须禁止 RSI。

paras.en: Woody Lee (responding to Chilson from above): [Alex Bores] defines what he means [by RSI] in the tweet.
paras.zh: Woody Lee（回应上文中 Chilson 的发言）：[Alex Bores] 在那条推文中定义了他[所说的 RSI]是什么意思。

paras.en: Neil Chilson: That's not a definition that works in legislation.
paras.zh: Neil Chilson：这不是一个能在立法中奏效的定义。

paras.en: Dave Kasten: I often disagree with Neil, so I want to flag here that I STRONGLY agree with him: we desperately need a definition of RSI that has gone through a bunch of rounds of lawyers kicking its tires.
paras.zh: Dave Kasten：我经常与 Neil 意见相左，所以我想在此表明，我**强烈**赞同他：我们迫切需要给 RSI 下一个定义，而且这个定义必须经过律师们多轮反复推敲检验。

paras.en: You're a law student, want to get cited for forever? Write this as your journal note.
paras.zh: 你是法学院学生，想被永久引用吗？把这个写成你的期刊论文吧。

paras.en: Saul Munn: wdyt of @testingham et al's definition of 'self-sustaining acceleration'?
paras.zh: Saul Munn：你觉得 @testingham 等人对“自我维持加速”（self-sustaining acceleration）的定义怎么样？

paras.en: Dave Kasten: Seems interesting, but not leg text by a long shot
paras.zh: Dave Kasten：看起来挺有意思，但远不是法律文本。

paras.en: It is probably going to be impossible to come up with a definition that will stop RSI at an early enough stage that such a law stays relevant to what happens next, and also avoids hitting anything that is not RSI. The blast radius will not be zero.
paras.zh: 我们很可能无法提出这样一种定义：它既能在足够早的阶段阻止 RSI，使相关法律对后续发展仍具相关性，又能避免误伤任何并非 RSI 的事物。其波及范围（blast radius）不会为零。

paras.en: The good news is that the blast radius can be things that RSI skeptics mostly say will not happen either way. If they are in good faith, they should be happy to draw lines in the sand that they do not expect anyone to be able to cross.
paras.zh: 好消息是，波及范围可以落在那些 RSI 怀疑论者大多认为无论如何都不会发生的事情上。如果他们出于善意，就应当乐于划下他们并不指望任何人能够越过的界线。

paras.en: This is similar to the talk of 'pacing the frontier.' Those calling to Pace the Frontier want to go at High Speed rather than Ludicrous Speed. Those who are against it want to ensure we go at Medium Speed rather than Low Speed, would love High Speed, and are scared of pausing entirely. It is easy to see how a deal there could be win-win.
paras.zh: 这类似于关于“为前沿定速”（pacing the frontier）的讨论。呼吁为前沿定速的人希望以高速（High Speed）而非疯狂速度（Ludicrous Speed）前进。反对者则希望确保我们以中速（Medium Speed）而非低速（Low Speed）前进，他们乐见高速，但害怕完全暂停。不难看出，双方在此达成协议可以是双赢的。

paras.en: Now more than ever, we need to prepare for scenarios where the critical events happen in 2027 or 2028. It might not play out that way, but it very well might.
paras.zh: 如今我们比以往任何时候都更需要为关键事件发生在 2027 年或 2028 年的情景做好准备。事情未必会如此发展，但完全有可能。
